Sports.title: Tsunoda ‘wasn’t hugely disappointed’ when Red Bull dropped him last year | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Yuki Tsunoda said he didn’t feel especially disappointed when Red Bull dropped him at the end of last season.

Red Bull promoted him to their top team at the third round of last season but chose not to extend his contract for 2026.

“When I got told, I still remember, I didn’t feel that much of a huge disappointment or devastated feeling,” Tsunoda told the official F1 channel. “Obviously I was still disappointed and pretty sad that I’m not driving next year, but it’s not like I didn’t expect it.”

Tsunoda said the pressure had been so intense over the second half of last year “I was never able to kind of breathe out much.” Red Bull told him at the penultimate round in Qatar he would be replaced at the end of the year.

While his team mate Max Verstappen went into the final round of the season with a chance to win the world championship, Tsunoda had the largest ever points deficit to a team mate in F1 history. Despite that, he said he could not have tried harder to improve his performance.

“I fought really hard,” he said. “I fought more than ever in that 2025 year. And even if I look back now, I don’t have much regret.

“I gave everything and the outcome is something I didn’t like, obviously, what I heard in Qatar. But honestly, I just gave it everything and okay, if that’s the outcome, yes, I have to accept it.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“It was something that I had to think about in the coming weeks or coming time. But still there was the Abu Dhabi race and still Max was fighting for the championship so my focus was still in Abu Dhabi to make the team happy and help Max as much as possible.”

Despite spending almost the entire season with the team, Tsunoda said he still didn’t understand Red Bull’s RB21 at the end of the year.

“Normally I’m able to understand the car, what I’m driving, what kind of characteristics, obviously [by the] end of the year,” he said.

“But it feels like even after Abu Dhabi I didn’t know what kind of car I was driving. I still don’t understand what was the issue and what kind of things made me struggle to learn about this car and get used to the car.

“I thought the confidence was there, but some races I just somehow lost confidence. I still don’t understand about the car, to be honest.”

Tsunoda said his efforts to emulate Verstappen’s approach to driving Red Bull’s car were not successful.

“One thing about myself, I think if I say completely honestly, is I have a big enough ego to not change my driving style,” he said. “I know what I’m doing in terms of driving and I believe in myself.

“So I never try to change my driving to other drivers even though that driver is competitive and fast. Obviously for Max, it’s a different case, he’s a world champion, he’s proved a lot of things.

“I still learned a lot of things from his driving, so still my core driving is the same, and then sometimes probably [that was the] first year out of any years since I started that I thought about changing my driving style and trying to do something similar to Max.

“But in my perspective, if I just look at data, I didn’t really see a huge difference in terms of driving. What I did most, and what I think now is the biggest mistake last year, was to try to replicate the set-up of what he’s doing.”

Tsunoda found Verstappen’s set-ups tended to exaggerate the handling traits he was already experiencing.

“Even though knowing that sometimes if I felt the car was very oversteery, Max’s car in theory made the car worse – more sensitive in the direction change or made the car slide more – I tended to choose that set-up, even though I was already struggling with this oversteer.

“It could happen sometimes the opposite way as well, even though I was struggling with understeer, and his car was more understeery, I tried to kind of replicate that.”

Sports.title: Monaco to hold first sprint race as F1 increases total to 10 on 2027 calendar | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 has announced its calendar for the 2027 season and increased the total number of sprint events to 10.

The 2027 F1 calendar will therefore include a record total of 34 races.

Despite concerns over the viability of racing in the Middle East, the championship has announced its 2027 season will begin and end with back-to-back rounds in the region.

The championship will open and close with sprint events in Bahrain and Abu Dhabi. This year’s Bahrain Grand Prix has been relocated to Malaysia due to the ongoing war in Iran, but Formula One Management says next year’s season-opener will take place at the Bahrain International Circuit.

Saudi Arabia’s Jeddah Corniche Circuit, which was dropped from this year’s calendar due to the war, is slated to hold the second round of the season.

The status of this year’s season-ending races in Qatar and Abu Dhabi remains in doubt. Formula 1 CEO Stefano has previously indicated a decision on whether those events will go ahead will be announced in mid-September, but F1’s statement on its 2027 calendar made no reference to the situation.

The cancellation of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix reduced the total number of events on this year’s calendar from 24 to 23. Providing all next year’s events take place, the calendar will return to a total of 24 rounds. As previously announced, Zandvoort in the Netherlands and the Circuit de Catalunya in Spain will lose their events, while new rounds in Portugal and Turkey join the calendar.

The total number of sprint events will increase from six to 10 next year. Although F1 originally announced the format would be used at “tracks with great overtaking potential”, next year’s calendar includes a sprint event at Monte-Carlo in Monaco, widely regarded as the hardest track to overtake on.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Four other venues will also hold sprint events for the first time: Bahrain, Melbourne in Australia, Suzuka in Japan and Yas Marina in Abu Dhabi. For the first time the opening race of the season will be a sprint race and the final round will also be a sprint event.

None of the 24 events clash with the Indianapolis 500, Le Mans 24 Hours or Nurburgring 24 Hours.

Sports.title: Stats: Mercedes equal Ferrari as F1’s most successful engine builders by race wins | 2026 Spanish Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Mercedes’ new star driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli delivered a milestone moment for the manufacturer with his victory in the Spanish Grand Prix.

Antonelli’s latest triumph was the 251st victory for a Mercedes-powered car in the history of the world championship. It puts them level with the most famous and historic name in the series, Ferrari.

Mercedes have achieved this despite contesting far fewer grands prix than their rivals. Both were active in the fifties, but Mercedes disappeared for four decades after the horrific deaths of the 1955 Le Mans 24 Hours.

Since their return with McLaren in the nineties, Mercedes have consistently been a force to be reckoned with. Ferrari dominated the early noughts but after Mercedes returned with their own factory team they enjoyed an unprecedented run of success the following decade.

Although the factory team had a difficult few seasons prior to this year, McLaren’s return to form helped to sustain the winning rate of their engine division. With Mercedes back on form this year, it has long seemed inevitable they would catch and eventually equal Ferrari’s tally:

*Season in progress

However Mercedes’ works team still lags far behind Ferrari’s in terms of total wins. McLaren scored more than 100 of the victories powered by Mercedes engines, while Brawn GP (2009) and Racing Point (2020) also contributed to Mercedes’ tally.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

In contrast, only a single race has ever been won by a Ferrari customer team: Sebastian Vettel’s 2008 Italian Grand Prix victory for Toro Rosso:

Mercedes’ record-equalling win came courtesy of Antonelli’s eighth career victory. That gives him as many as 1967 world champion Denny Hulme, plus Jacky Ickx and Daniel Ricciardo. It’s also one more than his team mate George Russell has scored.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Russell netted the 12th fastest lap of his career. That puts him level with rival Sergio Perez, as well as multiple world champions Alberto Ascari and Jack Brabham, plus Rene Arnoux and Juan Pablo Montoya.

Max Verstappen remains yet to score a win this season, but did claim second place in his 250th appearance in a grand prix weekend. He should make his 250th start in Singapore.

Lewis Hamilton failed to score for the first time this year. He was the last remaining driver to have taken points at every weekend and hadn’t finished outside the top six until his brake failure on Sunday.

For the first time since 2012, Spain held two rounds of the world championship. That year saw the final appearance of Valencia’s street track, an unloved venue which the Madring drew immediate comparisons with.

The Madring is the seventh different Spanish circuit to host F1. It joins Pedralbes, Jarama, Montjuich Park, Jerez, the Circuit de Catalunya and Valencia. France has also hosted F1 at seven different tracks but the only country with more grand prix venues is the USA, with 12.

There was little for the home crowd to celebrate in Madrid, however: Fernando Alonso and Carlos Sainz Jnr collided with each other and neither spent a single lap inside the top 10.

Sports.title: ‘Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers’ championship’ admits Russell | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli’s closest championship rival admits he does not have a realistic chance of beating him to the title this year.

George Russell lies 81 points behind his team mate with 233 available over the remaining rounds. He hasn’t gained on Antonelli since the British Grand Prix two months ago.

Russell finished fifth in Sunday’s race at the Madring, almost half a minute behind his race-winning team mate, after making a second pit stop. But after struggling with his car earlier in the season, Russell says recent rounds have gone better.

“It has been a more positive couple of races even though the result was far from great today,” said Russell on Sunday. “But it’s kind of the story of the season.

“I just need to focus on the performance and keep trying to help the team. We’re obviously in a great place to win the constructors’ [championship]. Realistically I’m not in the fight for the drivers and that just allows me just to focus on race-by-race and trying to focus on just getting some good results.”

Russell led the championship after the first two rounds but Antonelli moved ahead at the Japanese Grand Prix. He scored his eighth win on Sunday while Russell only has two victories so far this season.

Antonelli said he will not relent as he bids to clinch the world championship. “It’s great, but we’ve just got to keep pushing, keep delivering the results and just trying to do the best job I can whenever I go on track,” he said.

“Because of course, yes, I have a big lead, but you never know what can happen. So I just need to be ready for anything and keep maximising every opportunity I get, and then we’ll see where we end up at the end of the year.”

Sports.title: Isaac Cruz Uses Nestor Bravo as Gateway to Ryan Garcia
Sports.content:
Isaac Cruz knows beating Nestor Bravo is only the minimum requirement Saturday night. He needs a dominant performance to preserve his place among the opponents Ryan Garcia is considering for December or January.

“This fight means a lot to me. This fight can be something that pushes my career forward. I have to win to go on and face the big names,” Cruz said during Thursday’s final press conference. “My mind is fully focused on Nestor Bravo. That’s the only thing I’m thinking of. I want the fans to be the biggest winner of the night.”

Bravo’s size makes that audition less comfortable than it looks. Cruz is around 5 foot 4, while Bravo is a rangy 5 foot 9. A steady jab, lateral movement, and clinching can leave Cruz lunging from too far away and swinging at empty space.

That is where Cruz’s first fight under Eddy Reynoso becomes interesting. Reynoso teaches counterpunching, upper body movement, and controlled distance, but Cruz built his reputation by overwhelming opponents with pressure. If he becomes too cautious while waiting for clean counters, Bravo may dictate the pace from outside.

Reynoso does his best work with fighters who have natural counter-punching instincts, good punch placement, and the patience to pick clean shots from mid-range. Think of Canelo Alvarez, Oscar Valdez, or Andy Ruiz when he was in that camp. Reynoso teaches a fighter to sit down on their base, slip incoming fire with subtle upper-body movement, and explode with lethal, compact counters. Pitbull Cruz is built on the complete opposite side of the spectrum.

His entire ring identity is predicated on crude forward aggression, raw physical pressure, and throwing wide, overhand bombs to break an opponent’s spirit. He is essentially a wrecking ball in a small package. He does not set traps; he does not control distance with a measured jab, and he has never shown the foot speed or angles needed to outbox anyone who knows how to move.

History shows that trying to completely rewrite a mature fighter’s ring identity in his late twenties usually produces hesitation rather than polish. When a pure brawler tries to think too much in the ring, he loses the one attribute that made him dangerous in the first place: reckless, suffocating intensity. Jose Valenzuela exposed the limits of the one-gear style, and Lamont Roach proved Cruz can be frustrated by simple ring IQ and lateral movement. But the idea that Reynoso can teach a 5’4″ brawler to suddenly box like Juan Manuel Marquez or slip and counter like prime Canelo is unrealistic.

At best, Reynoso might tighten up Cruz’s guard inside the pocket, get him to work the body with more discipline, and teach him not to square up completely when closing the distance. Beyond that, trying to force Cruz into being a slick technician will just make him second-guess himself. Against a rangy boxer like Nestor Bravo, any hesitation from Cruz will make him look slow and completely lost.

José Valenzuela already showed how disciplined movement can frustrate Cruz. Lamont Roach also gave him problems without agreeing to the close-range fight Cruz prefers. Cruz claims the Roach performance proved he is more than a pressure fighter. Bravo gives him another opportunity to support that argument.

A close decision will retain Cruz’s interim WBC light welterweight title without strengthening his Ryan sales pitch. Ryan just stopped Conor Benn at welterweight and holds major physical advantages over Cruz. Teofimo Lopez and Devin Haney also offer Ryan larger commercial fights.

Cruz therefore needs more than a victory. He must create enough demand to stop Ryan from treating him as a secondary option. Bravo is his gateway to another major payday, but only a forceful performance keeps that door open.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua Targets December 11
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua are now being lined up to fight on December 11 in Cardiff. The date remains provisional because organizers still need to complete the permit process and other administrative work.

“Per a source with direct involvement, #JoshuaFury, if all is 100% buttoned up, will be on Dec. 11 in Cardiff. Still will take some time to wrap up the bureaucracy of getting permits in place,” Dan Rafael reported.

November 28 and December 4 were also discussed. Moving the fight onto a Friday shows how awkward the planning has become for an event intended to restore British interest in two former heavyweight champions.

The broadcast schedule may explain the unusual choice. A Friday avoids some of the major football and American sports competition found on Saturdays, but it transfers the burden onto ticket buyers. December 11 is a regular working day, forcing many traveling supporters to miss work and pay for accommodation.

The situation becomes far worse if broadcasters demand an extremely late ring walk for the American audience. Trains will not run throughout the night, hotel prices will climb, and thousands of spectators may be stranded in central Cardiff after leaving the stadium.

Permits may become the hardest part. Cardiff officials must consider policing, alcohol sales, noise restrictions and the movement of tens of thousands of people during the early morning hours. “Bureaucracy” may sound routine, but granting permission for a stadium crowd to empty onto the streets long after midnight presents a genuine safety issue.

The extra two weeks also do little to answer the competitive questions. Fury will have been inactive for almost two years after looking shopworn in his second loss to Oleksandr Usyk. His legs no longer carried him through sustained exchanges as comfortably as they once did.

Joshua’s brief knockout of Jake Paul did nothing to test his stamina, defense or response to legitimate heavyweight power. Neither man has recently endured a serious fight against an elite heavyweight.

Fury vs. Joshua will sell through name recognition and old rivalry, but the timing reflects what the matchup has become. A fight once meant to decide heavyweight supremacy is now being forced through late-hour permits and Friday scheduling while both fighters approach 40.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Return Targeted for David Benavidez Card
Sports.content:
Vergil Ortiz Jr. may end a wasted year by fighting on David Benavidez’s December 12 card. The opponent and weight have not been revealed, leaving the value of his comeback dependent on whom he faces and which division he chooses.

“Per sources, one of the possible spots for the return of Vergil Ortiz is for him to fight on the same card with David Benavidez on Dec. 12,” said Dan Rafael on X. “Would put two of the best and most entertaining fighters in boxing on the same show if it is finalized.”

Ortiz has not fought since stopping Erickson Lubin in November 2025. His contract dispute and lawsuit with Golden Boy Promotions consumed more than a year of his athletic prime while the 154-pound division continued without him.

Fighting beneath Benavidez would show how much ground Ortiz surrendered. He previously headlined events as a Texas attraction. He would now be accepting a supporting role to reintroduce himself without carrying the promotional burden of the entire card.

That may be practical, but it is still a demotion. The Lubin knockout once gave Ortiz significant leverage for a major fight with Jaron Ennis. Thirteen months of inactivity weakened that position while Ennis strengthened his own standing.

Ortiz also faces a difficult decision over weight. His past struggles at welterweight were severe, and making 154 pounds after a long absence will place his conditioning under scrutiny. Moving to middleweight would relieve the cut but take him away from the fights that made his comeback commercially interesting.

Choosing an opponent presents another problem. A dangerous contender such as Serhii Bohachuk or Charles Conwell would be a major gamble after the layoff. Pairing Ortiz with an obscure journeyman would turn the date into little more than paid sparring.

The December card can begin repairing the damage, but Ortiz needs more than activity. He needs a credible opponent and a performance strong enough to remind the division why Ennis against Ortiz once felt unavoidable.

Sports.title: British Boxing Board Creates New 187-Pound Division
Sports.content:
The British Boxing Board of Control has approved a 187-pound weight class to bridge the punishing jump between light heavyweight and cruiserweight. The problem is that anyone winning its British title will have nowhere to advance internationally.

Named light cruiserweight, the division begins January 1, 2027. Fighters can compete for Area, English, Celtic and British championships, but none of the four major sanctioning bodies recognizes the category.

Trainer Joe Gallagher pushed the proposal after watching boxers struggle with the 25-pound jump from 175 to 200.

“If you look at the smaller weight classes, they go up by three or four pounds until you get up to featherweight,” Gallagher said, as quoted by talkSPORT.

Adam Booth, Andy Lee, Jamie Moore, Pat Barrett and Robert McCracken also supported the change.

The safety case is stronger than the argument behind the WBC’s 224-pound bridgerweight division. Heavyweight has no upper limit, making bridgerweight feel like an extra championship created without a pressing need. A natural 190-pound fighter faces a harsher choice: drain himself to 175 or meet cruiserweights who may enter the ring near 215 after rehydrating.

Yet the new division leads directly into a domestic cul de sac. Winning a British championship traditionally prepares a fighter for European and world competition. A light cruiserweight champion must eventually squeeze back to 175 or bulk up to 200, defeating the purpose of the new category.

Promoters also have little reason to build headliners at 187. The division cannot produce a recognized world champion, much less a unified or undisputed title fight. Broadcasters already have difficulty explaining boxing’s collection of divisions and secondary belts.

There is also a danger that ordinary light heavyweights will chase easier honors at 187, weakening both domestic fields rather than protecting truly undersized cruiserweights.

Britain can test the idea, but its survival depends on international adoption. Without support from at least one major sanctioning body, light cruiserweight may become a British title with no road beyond it.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Derision Exposes Fear Of Relentless Zuffa Machine
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn is gloating because Zuffa Boxing paid a massive premium to snatch Conor Benn, only to watch their expensive acquisition get dismantled inside two rounds. Ryan Garcia’s right hand exposed Benn’s limits at the elite world level, leaving Zuffa holding the bag on a fighter whose marketability took a direct hit.

Hearn claims the Garcia-Benn event generated an $8 million gate but still lost heavily because of the money invested in the card and Benn.

“The show would have lost a lot of money, but that’s the investment that they’re making,” Hearn told The Stomping Ground. “They’ve absolutely done their conkers on Conor Benn. They never signed Conor Benn to make it work for their business. They signed Conor Benn as a personal vendetta against me. But that’s just amateur hour. One of the biggest mistakes you can ever make in business is to make emotional decisions to try and get one up on somebody else.”

Hearn is looking at Zuffa’s losses through the narrow lens of an old-school boxing promoter who relies on quarterly margins to survive, which completely misses how venture-backed outfits take over an industry.

In traditional boxing, promoters run lean. Every single show has to balance the books, or someone gets hurt financially. Matchroom operates on that grind, relying on ticket sales, local sponsorships, and regional broadcast rights to scrape out a profit margin. Naturally, Hearn looks at Zuffa dropping eight figures in fighter purses to generate an eight-million-dollar gate and assumes it was a financial catastrophe.

Corporate combat sports works under a completely different rulebook. When Endeavor and TKO Group jump into a new space, they play the long game. They operate the exact same playbook Silicon Valley tech firms and early UFC ownership used. You take heavy losses on purpose during the introductory phase to achieve rapid customer acquisition, establish brand authority, and box out legacy players.

Zuffa was never measuring success on whether September 12 turned a net profit at the box office. They bought their way to the center of the sport overnight. They packed out T-Mobile Arena, secured a premier broadcast slot on Paramount Plus, put on massive social media numbers, and proved they can mount a legitimate Vegas blockbuster.

More importantly, it sent a message to the entire boxing locker room. Fighters saw Benn pull an enormous paycheck; they saw first-class production, and they realized Zuffa has the financial muscle to outbid anyone. That type of institutional upheaval cannot be evaluated on a single night ticket stub balance sheet. Hearn might feel vindicated because Benn was stopped in the second round, but treating an intentional market acquisition budget as an amateur mistake shows he fundamentally underestimates the machine he is up against.

Sports.title: Conor Benn Trapped in Eubank Trilogy After Ryan Garcia Loss
Sports.content:
Conor Benn hit the treadmill immediately to show defiance, but no amount of roadwork fixes reckless fundamentals. The tape from Las Vegas showed a fighter whose aggression outran his technique, walking right into Ryan Garcia’s right hand with zero defensive responsibility. Running miles will not teach head movement.

Moving back up to settle the score with Chris Eubank Jr. is the only move that makes business sense. Boiling down to 146 pounds clearly drained Benn, and ballooning more than thirty pounds overnight to 178.4 proved his welterweight days are finished. Returning to 160 pounds eliminates that dangerous weight drain while salvaging his earning power.

A third meeting with Eubank carries built-in domestic demand that an ordinary tune-up cannot generate. With the series split at one win apiece, both men need each other to secure stadium gates and massive paydays. Taking a lesser fight risks getting exposed for a fraction of the purse, while a trilogy clash lets Benn cash in on family rivalry before his market value slips any further.

Conor Benn is almost certainly lining up the trilogy because the math leaves him no other choice. Nobody is handing out eight-figure checks for him to fight a run-of-the-mill middleweight contender in an empty arena.

Zuffa Boxing did not sign Benn to bankroll low-level rebuilding bouts. Dana White runs an outfit built entirely on numbers, event visibility, and immediate return. Dropping $10 million on Benn to face some unranked middleweight who cannot sell tickets makes zero financial sense. Benn does not command American pay-per-view numbers on his own name, and after getting blasted out inside two rounds by Ryan Garcia, his leverage took a massive hit.

The entire middleweight division is a commercial desert right now outside of Chris Eubank Jr. None of the titleholders carry the domestic box office appeal needed to justify Benn’s recent pay scale. If Benn signs to face someone like Janibek Alimkhanuly or Carlos Adames, the purse shrinks drastically while the physical danger skyrockets against seasoned punchers at 160 pounds.

That leaves Eubank Jr. as the sole cash cow left on the board. The score is tied, the family storyline still sells out British football stadiums, and the promotional hook practically writes itself. Both fighters know they need each other to secure that tier of compensation. Benn can jump right back into a mega-event, skip the embarrassing pay cut of an off-camera tune-up, and grab one more gigantic purse before the hype runs dry.

A traditional rebuild against modest opposition sounds sensible on paper, but that path closed long ago. A twenty-nine-year-old fighter with virtually no amateur background would normally take a step back, face unranked opposition, and quietly fix the defensive blunders Ryan Garcia exploited.

That patient route vanished once the massive paychecks arrived. Benn banked millions against Regis Prograis, Ryan, and two meetings with Chris Eubank Jr. Stepping down from stadium headliners to small-hall cards with tiny paydays is nearly impossible for a fighter used to generational wealth.

Strip away the marketing, and Benn remains the flawed prospect who labored through close calls against fringe fighters early on. He never inherited his father’s natural frame, chilling power, or granite chin, traits Nigel Benn needed to survive brutal warfare at 160 and 168 pounds.

Benn cannot afford a multi-year apprenticeship. He has too much money to accept peanut purses on untelevised shows, yet too many technical holes to take on elite contenders without getting hurt.

Returning to Eubank Jr. is the only move that keeps the money train rolling. The rivalry is tied, the public still buys the storyline, and the gate receipts remain enormous. Running on a treadmill makes for fine social media content, but it changes nothing about his reality. Benn has backed himself into a corner, and a third meeting with Eubank is the only door left open to another monster check.

Sports.title: Jaron Ennis Offers Terence Crawford’s Greatest Prime Test
Sports.content:
Eddie Hearn admits Terence Crawford never defeated an elite fighter in their prime, and that assessment exposes the truth about Crawford’s carefully constructed record. Jaron “Boots” Ennis represents the hungry monster Crawford spent his entire career sidestepping.

“I don’t think Crawford got to fight many elite or generational greats who were in their prime during his career,” Hearn said to Matchroom Boxing. “Well, he can do one here with Boots. Crawford, what he has is unbelievable self-belief, and he is adamant he beats Boots, and Boots is adamant he beats Terence Crawford.”

Hearn points out Crawford rarely fought prime generational talent. Crawford claims he dismantles Boots easily, while Ennis insists Crawford cannot survive him. Hearn is playing promotional games, but his critique strips away the manufactured myth surrounding Crawford’s legacy.

Examining Crawford’s biggest victories reveals a parade of compromised opposition. Errol Spence Jr. was a damaged fighter after a high-speed rollover car wreck and multiple eye surgeries. Shawn Porter arrived with one foot out the door, retiring in his locker room immediately after the stoppage. Kell Brook had surgically repaired eye sockets. Amir Khan was a chinny relic whose best days ended a decade earlier. Ricky Burns and Julius Indongo were paper champions who offered zero resistance.

The warning signs emerged against Israil Madrimov. Crawford struggled with Madrimov’s power, timing, and ring movement, escaping with a disputed decision that left the crowd howling. Crawford then cashed out against a faded 35-year-old Canelo Alvarez who lacked the footwork or hand speed to make Crawford pay.

Instead of defending the super middleweight belts, Crawford beat a hasty path to retirement. The wolves were circling at 168 pounds. Osleys Iglesias, Christian Mbilli, and Lester Martinez were waiting to unleash physical punishment. Those killers do not care about pound-for-pound accolades. They bring raw power, prime legs, and brutal pressure.

Old-school warriors stood their ground, traded leather, and accepted the challenge against hungry young contenders. Crawford protected his record, collected his checks, and exited before someone stripped him of his mystique.

Boots Ennis wants Crawford right now. Ennis is 29, ferocious, and operating at peak physical capacity. Crawford talks about how easily he handles Boots on social media, yet he remains safely parked in retirement. Taking shots from the safety of an armchair is easy. Stepping inside the ropes against a prime killer is something Crawford avoided his entire life.

Sports.title: Rocky Marciano Bleeds, Then Crushes Ezzard Charles
Sports.content:
Rocky Marciano defended the heavyweight championship against Ezzard Charles on September 17, 1954, surviving a gruesomely split nose before producing one of the most savage finishes of his career.

Their second fight at Yankee Stadium followed a punishing 15 round meeting three months earlier. Charles had given Marciano his hardest title defense, cutting his left eye and controlling long stretches with cleaner boxing. Marciano rallied to win a unanimous decision, but Charles had earned another chance.

Rain delayed the rematch twice. When the fighters finally met, Marciano carried a 46-0 record and the undisputed championship into the ring. Charles was trying to become the first former heavyweight champion to regain the crown.

Charles came in at 192½ pounds, seven pounds heavier than he had been for the first fight. His camp may have decided that another 15 rounds with Marciano was too punishing to repeat. The additional weight suggested Charles planned to hurt the champion early, but it pushed him toward a power punching fight that suited Marciano far better.

Charles landed cleanly in the opening round, but Marciano dropped him with a right hand in the second. The challenger became increasingly cautious after rising. Marciano crowded him through the middle rounds, attacking the arms, ribs and head while Charles searched for room to box.

The extra weight failed to produce greater authority in Charles’s punches. It mainly gave Marciano a slower target.

Marciano’s pressure also came with a steady supply of illegal punches. Whenever Charles bent forward to escape, Marciano chopped right hands onto the back of his head. Slow-motion footage shows this was not an isolated blow caused by Charles turning at the wrong instant. It happened repeatedly in nearly every round, often directly in front of referee Al Berl.

Charles’s low defensive posture created the opening, but the back of his head remained an illegal target. Marciano also used his glove laces and heel, struck low, and continued punching after the bell without losing a point. Berl allowed him to fight with enormous freedom inside.

The fight changed in the sixth when Marciano came out of a clinch with his left nostril split deeply enough to leave part of it hanging loose. Blood poured down his face. Charles’s corner immediately told him to attack the injury, knowing a medical stoppage offered his clearest route to the championship.

Marciano also had a cut near his left eye, but he kept advancing. By the end of the seventh, he had Charles reeling at the bell.

His corner wanted body punches in the eighth. Marciano rejected the advice.

“I was spilling too much blood, and they might have stopped it. I like my title too much to lose it on account of a little blood. I don’t knock ’em out in the body. I knock ’em out on the chin.”

That decision showed more than courage. Marciano understood that he no longer had time to break Charles down through the body. He abandoned his usual attritional attack and concentrated everything upstairs, calculating that one clean right would protect his championship faster than several more minutes of body work.

A long right dropped Charles for a four count. After Charles rose, a left hook and another right sent him down again. He barely beat the count, but Berl stopped the fight at 2:36.

Charles had fought Marciano for 23 brutal rounds across two bouts. He had outboxed him, cut him, and torn open his nose, yet none of it stopped the champion from advancing. The psychological burden must have been enormous. Injuring Marciano only triggered a more desperate assault.

Still, the rabbit punches complicate the familiar story of Marciano overcoming blood through courage alone. His urgency was genuine, but Charles had absorbed repeated illegal shots to the back of the head. Berl’s tolerance turned every defensive bend from Charles into another opportunity for Marciano to club him.

The Ring named it the 1954 Fight of the Year. Marciano moved to 47-0 and later called Charles the toughest man he ever fought. His toughness and finishing instinct were extraordinary, but this was also a dirty performance protected by the permissive officiating of the era. Both truths belong in the story.

Ghana News.title: U.S. Trade and Development Agency, C-Squared Africa sign deal to expand affordable digital connectivity in Ghana
Ghana News.content:
The U.S. Trade and Development Agency (USTDA) and C-Squared Africa have signed an agreement for a feasibility study on the deployment of fibre-optic cables along Ghana’s existing electricity infrastructure.

The agreement was signed during the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Forum 2026, jointly organised by the American Chamber of Commerce, Ghana (AmCham Ghana), the U.S. Embassy in Accra, the U.S. Commercial Service and USTDA.

The forum, held at the Marriott Hotel in Accra on Wednesday, September 9, 2026, brought together government officials, industry leaders and technology partners to discuss Ghana’s AI ambitions under the theme, “AI Deployment and Diffusion: Emerging Opportunities and Supportive Policy.”

The feasibility study is expected to support the expansion of affordable and reliable digital connectivity across the country by exploring the use of existing electricity infrastructure for fibre deployment.

The signing was witnessed by U.S. Embassy Chargé d’Affaires Rolf Olson and Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, Samuel Nartey George.

Ghana outlines AI ambitions

Speaking at the forum, Mr George outlined the government’s vision for artificial intelligence under the National AI Strategy launched by President John Dramani Mahama on April 24, 2026.

He said Ghana’s approach to AI is anchored in national data sovereignty, local capacity building and talent development.

The Minister also stressed the importance of partnerships that can transfer technical skills and create sustainable value for Ghanaian businesses.

The forum featured discussions on Ghana’s AI infrastructure, market trends, regulation, data protection and public-sector procurement.

The infrastructure panel examined the connectivity, power and data-centre requirements needed to support the country’s AI ambitions, with representatives from ATC Ghana, the National Information Technology Agency (NITA), C-Squared and NEDCo.

A second panel focused on AI adoption among Ghanaian businesses, including the transition from experimentation to wider enterprise deployment.

Participants also highlighted the need for stronger institutional trust and governance, as well as AI solutions developed around Ghanaian data and business realities.

Focus on regulation and public-sector adoption

Discussions on regulation examined how Ghana’s data protection framework could respond to emerging AI-related issues, including consent, cross-border data transfers and automated decision-making.

Representatives from the Ministry of Communication, Digital Technology and Innovation, the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Telecoms Chamber participated in the session.

Another panel examined the procurement of AI technologies for public-sector deployment, with the Ghana Investment Fund for Electronic Communications (GIFEC), World Bank and Ghana Digital Acceleration Project (GDAP) contributing to discussions.

Participants considered ways to simplify public-sector technology procurement and discussed calls for a unified digital platform to make business licensing and regulatory compliance easier.

The forum concluded with remarks from Enid Kanor, Deputy Chair of AmCham Ghana’s Digital Committee and representative of ATC Ghana, followed by a networking reception.

Ghana News.title: We have at least 6 weeks of fuel cover – NPA boss calms supply fears
Ghana News.content:
The National Petroleum Authority (NPA) says Ghana currently has at least six weeks of fuel cover, dismissing concerns that the country could face an imminent shortage amid tightening global petroleum supplies.

NPA Chief Executive Officer, Godwin Edudzi Tamakloe, said the available stocks, combined with fuel cargoes currently at sea, provide a significant buffer for the domestic market.

“Currently, we have not less than 6 weeks of cover. Not less,” he said on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday.

He was responding to concerns over Ghana’s fuel supply outlook following recent reports of tighter global supplies and reduced fuel exports to some countries in the sub-region.

Asked whether the level of stocks was enough, Mr Tamakloe pointed to the number of vessels currently on the high seas carrying petroleum products.

“And if you look at the number of vessels even on the high seas, it is significant. So at this point, yes, I have some supply,” he said.

The NPA boss said his immediate concern was not the availability of fuel but the potential impact of international market conditions on prices.

“No, my major concern now is price,” he said.

Asked whether he expected supply problems within the next month, Mr Tamakloe was emphatic.

“Not at all,” he said.

He explained that developments in the international market were also prompting exporting countries to adjust their strategies, while pointing to the growing role of Nigeria’s Dangote refinery.

“Dangote is here,” he said to allay such fears.

His comments come as Ghana’s fuel market faces renewed pressure from global supply disruptions linked to conflicts and tighter availability of petroleum products.

The International Energy Agency has warned of a significant reduction in global oil supply in 2026, while refined fuel inventories have also come under pressure.

The developments have also coincided with fresh increases in Ghana’s fuel price floors. From September 16, the NPA’s floor price rose to GH¢16 per litre for petrol and GH¢16.77 for diesel, with LPG set at GH¢10.97 per kilogramme.

Meanwhile, BOSTenergies has clarified that reductions in fuel exports to Burkina Faso and Mali do not indicate an imminent shortage in Ghana.

The company said the reduction was largely linked to revamp works at its Bolgatanga depot.

Mr Tamakloe also defended Ghana’s private-sector-led downstream petroleum architecture, saying the system was deliberately designed to encourage private-sector participation.

He acknowledged concerns that private operators could potentially exert pressure on government but said safeguards had been introduced.

“I think there are some buffers that we put in place to ensure that the 2014-2015 events do not happen again. And like I said, that’s a particular concern, a great concern, to the President of the Republic, so we don’t get to a point where the private sector can effectively hold the whole country to ransom,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Fiji declares HIV a national emergency as cases surge
Ghana News.content:
Fiji declares HIV a national emergency as cases surge

Fiji has declared a national emergency as HIV cases surge, and is expanding access to testing, treatment and prevention services.

About one in 60 adults in the tiny Pacific archipelago is now living with the bloodborne virus, compared with one in 167 five years ago, with a rising number of babies dying from HIV-related complications.

The nation of less than a million people saw 2,016 new diagnoses in 2025 alone, Health Minister Antonio Lalabalavu said, noting that "an outbreak-level response is no longer sufficient".

A spiralling trend of drug use, unsafe sex, needle sharing and "bluetoothing" underpins the epidemic, health experts and NGOs earlier told the BBC.

"Bluetoothing" or "hotspotting" refers to the dangerous practice where intravenous drug users inject the blood of already intoxicated individuals, which has fuelled a global HIV surge, especially in parts of Africa and in the Pacific.

One reason for its appeal is a cheaper high: multiple people can chip in for a single hit and share it among themselves. Another is the convenience of needing only one syringe, which are difficult to come by in Fiji.

One in 60 adults live with the bloodborne virus, with a rising number of babies dying from HIV-related complications

The Fijian government will introduce a syringe and needle programme as part of its response to the national crisis.

The country already has sufficient supplies of syringes and needles, Lalabalavu says, with legislative amendments to be introduced in parliament so that the programme can be rolled out.

The minister also urged people to come forward and get tested.

"No one should be ashamed, threatened, or excluded because of their HIV status," he said. "Stigma drives people away from the very services that can help them."

Of the 9,100 Fijians living with HIV in 2025, only 39% knew their HIV status and just 22% were accessing antiretroviral treatment, according to the Joint United Nations Programme on HIV and Aids (UNAIDS).

This stands in stark contrast to the global average, where 78% of people with HIV are accessing treatment.

Jason Mitchell, who leads the national HIV response taskforce, believes it will take "upwards of five years for [Fiji] to get on top of the epidemic".

"It's a long-term programme, it's not something like Covid that's turned around in two years. HIV is very different," he told ABC News is an interview.

The HIV epidemic has led to a strain on Fiji's health services, Mitchell said. "For a health system that's already struggling, to have people who should really be well because there's treatment available taking up beds in hospitals and sitting in outpatient... Our clinical services has really been under a lot of pressure."

UNAIDS has welcomed Fiji's emergency declaration, saying it signals the urgency needed to ramp up response to a higher level across government and society.

"It is also a stark reminder to the world that Aids is not over. HIV epidemics can change quickly, and countries need health and community systems that are ready to respond urgently," said the executive director of UNAIDS Winnie Byanyima.

Ghana News.title: Michelin-starred Seoul restaurant fined for using ants as garnish
Ghana News.content:
Most of the ants came from the US, with some coming from Thailand

A two Michelin-starred restaurant in Seoul has been fined for using ants as a dessert garnish.

The owner of Evett in the South Korean capital was fined 15 million won (£8,144; $10,965), while the company operating the restaurant was fined 10 million won for violating the Food Sanitation Act, local media report.

Ants are not among the 10 insect species approved for human consumption in the East Asian nation. The approved list includes grasshoppers, locusts and some silkworms.

Prosecutors had sought a one-year prison term for the restaurant's owner, as well as a 20 million won fine, but the judge took into account the owner's admission of the charge and lack of prior criminal record.

However, the judge is reported to have said that, in addition to violating food standards, heavy metals exceeding standards were detected in the ants when they were tested, meaning the "culpability is not light".

The owner was said to have been unaware that providing ants in food was prohibited in South Korea, as they are used as food elsewhere.

Their use as a topping for sorbets at Evett came to light after the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety found online reviews accompanied by photographs.

It said the owner had sprinkled three to five ants on certain dishes to give them a "sour taste" over nearly four years, amounting to approximately 49,000 ants used as a garnish.

Most of the ants were imported from the US, while some came from Thailand, the ministry said.

The owner had argued that they were used in a "small part" of the restaurant's 15-course menu and that diners were told they could opt for a non-ant alternative topping.

Ants are eaten and sometimes even valued as a delicacy in several Asian, African and Latin American cultures. Weaver ants and their eggs are used in Thai and Cambodian cooking, while in Colombia, queen ants are as prized as caviar.

The Michelin Guide considers a two-star establishment as one that does "excellent cooking" and is "worth a detour".

Ghana News.title: No politics behind fuel export reduction to Sahel – BOSTenergies
Ghana News.content:
BOSTenergies Limited says the reduction in fuel export volumes to Burkina Faso and Mali has nothing to do with politics, security or diplomatic considerations.

The clarification follows a Reuters report based on comments by BOSTenergies Managing Director Afetsi Awoonor during an energy conference in Bangkok.

Mr Awoonor was quoted as saying BOSTenergies was “managing our export business to ensure that we have enough for the country first.”

BOSTenergies, however, said the report created an inaccurate impression that Ghana was facing an imminent fuel shortage and had therefore reduced supplies to the two Sahelian countries.

The company stressed that there is no imminent fuel shortage in Ghana, and no rationing of available fuel has been implemented.

According to BOSTenergies, the reduction in regional exports is largely due to ongoing revamp works at its Bolgatanga depot, which serves as its main gateway to the Sahelian market.

The company said “No political, security, or diplomatic consideration played any role in this decision.”

Under normal operations, BOSTenergies transports fuel to the northern part of the country through an integrated network of pipelines and barges linking its depots from the south to the north.

This network enables the company to supply Burkina Faso and Mali at competitive prices while meeting its required profit margins.

With the Bolgatanga depot undergoing revamp and nearing completion, BOSTenergies said it has maintained regional supplies by transporting products from its coastal depot in Tema using Bulk Road Vehicles.

The company said this arrangement is being implemented while ensuring equitable access to fuel across demand zones nationwide.

BOSTenergies expects full regional supply capacity to be restored once the Bolgatanga depot revamp is completed.

The company said it remains committed to supporting regional fuel security through reliable and commercially sound supply arrangements.

It added that it is working with government and regulatory partners to expedite the completion of the Bolgatanga depot.

BOSTenergies also pledged to continue engaging the media and the public transparently on developments affecting Ghana’s downstream petroleum sector.

Ghana News.title: New iPhones, new features: Is it time to upgrade?
Ghana News.content:
Apple just held its biggest hardware event of the year, unveiling the iPhone 18 Pro, the iPhone 18 Pro Max, and its first-ever folding phone, the iPhone Duo. Within 48 hours, timelines had already split into two camps: "revolutionary" or "just another incremental release."

But the real story here isn't Apple's spec sheet. It's the pattern behind how Apple builds, and what that pattern quietly teaches about the right and wrong reasons to upgrade anything, phone or otherwise.

The Breakdown

Apple's approach to its first folding phone tells you almost everything about its playbook. Samsung and Huawei have been refining folding screens for years. Apple waited, watched what broke elsewhere, and arrived with a version engineered to fit tightly into its existing ecosystem rather than to win first-mover bragging rights. The iPhone Duo's hinge, its opening animation, and its software all feel deliberately smoothed over compared to earlier folding attempts on the market. Apple's pattern isn't inventing categories, it's arriving late and polished.

Put the Duo next to Samsung's Z Fold 8 or Huawei's Pura X, though, and the picture gets more complicated. Apple's foldable is heavier at 254 grams versus Huawei's 229. It's locked to eSIM only, while Huawei's Pura X still carries a physical SIM slot.

It caps multitasking at two apps side-by-side, while the Pura X handles more open at once. And it's priced well above both rivals, starting north of $1,999. Apple does win on pixel density, and arguably on how tightly the hardware locks into an ecosystem people already live in.

The iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max, meanwhile, carry the more incremental upgrades: a new mechanical aperture control on the camera, a faster A20 chip, deeper-reading health sensors on the Watch line, and modest battery gains; 35 hours on the Pro, 45 on the Pro Max.

None of that is nothing. But none of it changes daily life for someone who wasn't already pushing last year's phone to its limit.

What It Means

Strip away the launch-week noise and a simple principle emerges: hype is not an upgrade trigger. Need is. The signals that should actually move someone toward the iPhone 18 Pro, the Duo, or any new device are practical, not emotional. That is:

A phone that's visibly slowed down

A battery that can no longer survive a day without a power bank

A charging port or SIM setup that no longer matches where the world has moved

Repair costs creeping toward the price of a new device

A security update cliff that leaves you exposed.

Apple's own camera aperture control is a perfect example: genuinely useful to someone who shoots seriously, invisible to someone who doesn't know it exists.

There's also a quieter truth worth naming. Apple has talked about on-device private AI for several product cycles now, and each year the promise resets without much to show for it in daily use. Marketing timelines and delivery timelines are rarely the same thing. It's worth separating "announced" from "actually working" before it factors into any buying decision.

The Opportunity

For anyone building a career, a brand, or a business around content or technology, this is the leverage point: the same iPhone in two different hands produces two completely different outcomes, and the gap is almost entirely about skill and intent, not spec. That means the smartest investment isn't chasing Apple's newest release.

It is mastering the device already in your pocket until it stops being the bottleneck. Once a tool's capability is genuinely maxed out, upgrading stops being a flex and starts being a multiplier. That's the moment a new iPhone, or any new tool, pays for itself instead of just looking good in a photo.

The Next Move

Before the next upgrade, Apple's newest release or anything else, ask one honest question: is this solving a real limitation, or am I just responding to a launch?

If it's the former, invest with confidence and treat it as the business decision it is.

If it's the latter, hold on, and let the device you already own finish earning its keep.

The people who build real advantage aren't the ones with the newest iPhone, they're the ones who know exactly when a new one is actually worth the money.

Ghana News.title: German Development Cooperation, KOA partner to turn cashew apples into jobs, incomes and investment
Ghana News.content:
The German Development Cooperation has partnered with Swiss-Ghanaian company KOA to transform Ghana’s underutilised cashew apples into commercially viable products, creating additional income opportunities for farmers, women and rural enterprises.

The initiative, launched on Wednesday, September 16, 2026, seeks to reduce the large volumes of cashew apples left as waste after farmers harvest the nuts, while creating new opportunities for local processing, job creation and investment.

Cashew apples can account for up to 90 per cent of the fruit’s mass but are often left to rot in the field after the nuts are harvested.

Through KOA’s Community Mobile Processing Unit approach, the partnership will support communities to collect and process cashew apples closer to farms and produce cashew apple juice, concentrate and dried cashew apple products for local and European markets.

The model is designed to reduce post-harvest losses, create value closer to the source of the raw material and connect community-level production to growing markets.

The project will work with women’s groups, cooperatives and farmer organisations, with a focus on building practical processing skills, strengthening market linkages and developing a production model that can be replicated across cashew-producing communities.

Head of the Private Sector and Innovation Promotion (PSInno) Programme at GIZ Ghana, Arlett Stojanovic, said the partnership demonstrates how development initiatives can create commercial opportunities.

“This partnership is about demonstrating that development impact and commercial opportunity can reinforce each other. Using this underutilised resource is creating new opportunities for farmers and private-sector investment,” she said.

For farmers, the initiative is expected to provide an additional source of income from the same harvest, while women and community enterprises could take on roles in processing, quality management and value addition.

KOA’s Director of Production and Operations, Daniel Otu, said the company sees significant untapped potential in the cashew apple.

“We see the cashew apple not as a waste product, but as an untapped raw material with the potential to support an entirely new layer of value creation in Ghana’s cashew industry,” he said.

“By bringing processing closer to farmers, we can help communities capture more value from the cashew they already produce while building products that can compete in local and international markets,” he added.

The partnership also seeks to attract investors and businesses into the emerging segment of Ghana’s cashew value chain by demonstrating a commercially sustainable model that can be scaled by the private sector.

The initiative is being implemented through GIZ’s PSInno and the Market-Oriented Value Chains for Jobs and Growth in the ECOWAS Region (MOVE-ComCashew), in partnership with KOA Impact and with support from develoPPP on behalf of the German Federal Ministry for Economic Cooperation and Development (BMZ).

The partners believe that increasing the economic value of cashew apples could help Ghana’s cashew sector move beyond traditional kernel production and create additional value from resources already available in farming communities.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
