Ghana is drawing up a national space policy and plans to establish its first dedicated space institution. Foreign minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa set out the plan while hosting the astronaut Koichi Wakata in Accra on 15 September 2026.

What Was Announced

Foreign minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa said Ghana is formulating a national space policy. He also said the country intends to establish its first dedicated space institution.

He spoke while hosting the astronaut Koichi Wakata in Accra on 15 September 2026. Ablakwa framed the longer ambition as producing the first African astronaut from Ghana.

Who Koichi Wakata Is

Wakata has flown to space five times, making him one of the most experienced astronauts of his generation. He spent his career with Japan’s space agency before leaving it in 2024.

He is now chief technology officer for Asia Pacific at Axiom Space, an American company. That matters, because it means the visit is as much commercial as it is governmental.

What Ghana Has Already Flown

GhanaSat-1 was built by students at All Nations University working with the Kyushu Institute of Technology. It was developed under a multi-country small-satellite programme.

The satellite was deployed from the Japanese module of the International Space Station in 2017. Japan’s role was the deployment and the university partnership rather than the design.

Who Else Was in the Room

The foreign ministry’s chief director Khadija Iddrisu attended, alongside the Japanese ambassador Hiroshi Yoshimoto. The University of Ghana’s vice chancellor Nana Aba Appiah Amfo was also present.

The mix of a foreign ministry, an embassy and a university is the usual shape of early space cooperation. None of those parties builds spacecraft.

The Agreements Already in Place

Ghana’s space science institute signed an agreement with Axiom Space in March 2025. A separate memorandum on space business cooperation was signed at a Japan-Africa summit in Yokohama in August 2025.

Those are two different tracks with two different partners. Coverage has sometimes merged them, and they should be read separately.

Why a Policy Comes Before Anything Else

A national space policy sets out what a country wants from space activity and who is responsible for it. Without one, satellite projects sit inside whichever ministry happens to sponsor them.

An institution gives those activities a permanent home and a budget line. Both are prerequisites for anything beyond student projects.

What Space Capability Is Actually For

For most African countries the practical value of space is data rather than exploration. Earth observation supports agriculture, flood mapping, urban planning and mining oversight.

Ghana already uses satellite data bought from others. A domestic institution would change who controls access and cost rather than launching rockets.

The Astronaut Ambition in Perspective

Sending a national astronaut is expensive and depends entirely on a partner’s vehicle. It is a statement of intent rather than a technical programme.

Commercial operators now sell seats, which is why the ambition is being voiced in a room containing a commercial space executive. That is the realistic route if it happens.

What Is Not Yet Known

No timetable, budget or legal framework for the new institution has been published. Nor has a draft of the policy been released.

It is also unclear whether any commercial agreement followed the meeting. Neither side announced one.

What to Watch

Publication of the draft national space policy. That document would show whether the plan is about data or about prestige.

Watch also for a budget line in Ghana’s next appropriation. An institution without funding is an announcement.

More: Africa news and analysis, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Ghana announce?

That it is formulating a national space policy and plans to establish its first dedicated space institution.

Who visited Accra?

Koichi Wakata, a five-time space traveller who now leads Asia Pacific technology for Axiom Space.

Is Wakata still with Japan’s space agency?

No. He left it in 2024 and now works for an American company.

What is GhanaSat-1?

A small satellite built by All Nations University students with the Kyushu Institute of Technology, deployed from the International Space Station in 2017.

Has a budget been announced?

No. No timetable, budget or legal framework has been published.

What would a space institution do?

Most likely manage earth observation data for agriculture, flood mapping, planning and resource oversight.

Sources: Ghanaian foreign ministry engagements reported on 17 September 2026 by MyJoyOnline and Ecofin Agency; Ghana Space Science and Technology Institute agreements of March 2025 and August 2025.

World.title: Honduran scrap-gold dealer allegedly lured to Faber’s Road and shot dead for money
World.content:
Honduran scrap-gold dealer allegedly lured to Faber’s Road and shot dead for money

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Honduran national who regularly purchased scrap gold in Belize City was allegedly lured to the Faber’s Road area Wednesday evening before being shot and killed after a demand for money, police say.

Police responded to the shooting at around 6:20 p.m. and found 42-year-old Dennis Guevara suffering from gunshot injuries. He was rushed to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital, where he later succumbed.

According to investigators, Guevara routinely purchased scrap gold from people in the area and had reportedly been contacted by someone who asked to meet him there.

Police say that during the meeting, the person allegedly demanded money from Guevara before shooting him several times.

Authorities have not yet confirmed whether robbery was the motive for the killing.

Investigators are reviewing surveillance footage from the area and are working to identify and locate suspects.

World.title: U.S. Ambassador André Bauer personally delivers school bags to students in Santana Village
World.content:
U.S. Ambassador André Bauer personally delivers school bags to students in Santana Village

By Breaking Belize News Staff: United States Ambassador to Belize André Bauer personally handed out backpacks filled with school supplies to primary school students during a visit to Zion Park Methodist Primary School in Santana Village on Thursday.

Bauer was joined by locally employed staff of the U.S. Embassy in Belmopan for the distribution, which also included supplies for teachers. In photographs shared by the Embassy, the newly appointed ambassador is seen interacting directly with the children and handing backpacks to students.

The Embassy described the initiative as part of its continuing commitment to education and opportunity across Belize.

Thursday’s donation continues a years-long pattern of U.S. Embassy support for Belizean students. In 2022, the Embassy provided 500 backpacks containing school supplies to students of Carmelita and Santa Martha Government Schools in the Orange Walk District.

In 2016, the Embassy donated more than 150 backpacks to a back-to-school drive for children in residential care facilities; records from that initiative indicate then-Deputy Chief of Mission Adrienne Galanek participated in the distribution rather than then-Ambassador Carlos Moreno.

And Bauer is not the first U.S. ambassador to personally get involved in handing the bags to Belizean children. In January 2023, then-Ambassador Michelle Kwan personally distributed backpacks and school supplies during a visit to San Jose Government School in Orange Walk. News 5 reported Kwan describing the experience of “passing out school supplies, backpacks to the students,” while the Embassy’s contribution of school supplies was valued at approximately US$8,000.

Bauer was sworn in as U.S. Ambassador to Belize in August and recently began his assignment in the country.

World.title: International News: U.S.-Mexico trade talks advance
World.content:
International News: U.S.-Mexico trade talks advance

By Zoila Palma: U.S. President Donald Trump and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum spoke by phone Wednesday as the two countries continue negotiations aimed at reaching an agreement on trade, according to a U.S. official and a person familiar with the conversation.

The call comes as Washington and Mexico move closer to an agreement on the future of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA).

The two sources offered differing descriptions of the conversation.

The person familiar with the call, who spoke anonymously, described it as “so-so” and said new topics were introduced during the discussion, creating some uncertainty.

A U.S. official, also speaking anonymously, described the conversation as “constructive” and said the trade negotiations remain active and are moving in a positive direction, Politico reports.

Mexican officials believed the two sides were nearing an agreement addressing concerns surrounding the USMCA, the North American trade pact signed during Trump’s first term, according to the person familiar with the call. The ongoing review has involved increasingly detailed negotiations between Washington and Mexico over the future of the agreement.

The fourth round of formal U.S.-Mexico discussions has been rescheduled for September 28 and 29 in Washington. The talks follow a third round in July between Mexican officials and U.S. Trade Ambassador Jamieson Greer, where both sides reported progress on areas including automobiles, steel and aluminum, agriculture, labor and economic security.

World.title: Trees, Climate action and conservation: Ministry brings sustainability to Independence Day parade
World.content:
Trees, Climate action and conservation: Ministry brings sustainability to Independence Day parade

By Zoila Palma: The Ministry of Sustainable Development will join Belize’s 45th Independence Day celebrations in San Ignacio and Santa Elena, highlighting its efforts to promote a healthier, more resilient and sustainable Belize.

The Ministry will participate with an Independence Day float showcasing its departments, programmes and national initiatives.

Featured initiatives will include the One Million Trees Campaign, the “Bin It” campaign promoting responsible waste management, climate action and resilience, and water conservation.

The float will also highlight efforts in biodiversity and protected areas, the Carbon Market and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Through the initiatives, the Ministry aims to raise awareness about environmental stewardship, responsible resource management and the importance of building communities that can adapt to a changing climate.

World.title: Team Belize set for 5-match FIFA U-15 World Cup Qualification campaign
World.content:
Team Belize set for 5-match FIFA U-15 World Cup Qualification campaign

By Zoila Palma: Today, the Football Federation of Belize announced Team Belize’s qualification-stage match schedule for the FIFA U-15 World Cup & Festival 2026, which will take place in Azerbaijan from October 22–31, 2026.

Team Belize’s 5 qualification-stage matches will be played at the Hovsan Competition Complex. Belize has been drawn in Group F alongside Liberia, Curaçao, Morocco, the Philippines and Costa Rica.

Our Jaguars will open their campaign against Liberia on October 24, followed by two matches each on October 25 and 26.

TEAM BELIZE — MATCH SCHEDULE

Date Match Azerbaijan Time Belize Time Saturday, October 24, 2026 Liberia vs Belize 9:00 a.m. 11:00PM (Oct 23rd) Sunday, October 25, 2026 Belize vs Curaçao 2:30 p.m. 4:30AM Sunday, October 25, 2026 Morocco vs Belize 8:45 p.m. 10:45AM Monday, October 26, 2026 Philippines vs Belize 2:30 p.m. 4:30AM Monday, October 26, 2026 Belize vs Costa Rica 8:45 p.m. 10:45AM

Following the qualification stage, the competition schedule includes a rest day on October 27, with tournament-stage matches beginning October 28. Team Belize’s subsequent fixtures will be determined following qualification-stage results.

“Participation provides an important opportunity for Belize’s emerging footballers to gain international experience, compete against teams from different regions and proudly represent their country. It also supports the FFB’s continued commitment to youth football development,” FFB said.

The FFB calls on Belizeans at home and abroad to rally behind Team Belize as our young footballers prepare to wear the national colors on the world stage.

World.title: U.S. Ambassador visits Peace Corps Belize Headquarters
World.content:
U.S. Ambassador visits Peace Corps Belize Headquarters

By Zoila Palma: U.S. Ambassador Andre Bauer visited the Peace Corps Belize headquarters earlier this week, gaining firsthand insight into how Volunteers and staff work alongside Belizean communities to support education and youth development.

The visit highlighted grassroots efforts being carried out through partnerships with communities across Belize.

Ambassador Bauer’s engagement reflects his interest in seeing how the U.S.-Belize partnership translates into direct community-level impact.

The visit also provided an opportunity to learn more about the work of Peace Corps Volunteers and staff and their collaboration with Belizeans to address local development priorities.

World.title: International News: Canadian PM welcomes potential Canada-EU ‘Associate Member’ partnership
World.content:
International News: Canadian PM welcomes potential Canada-EU ‘Associate Member’ partnership

By Zoila Palma: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has welcomed the European Union’s proposal for Canada to become the bloc’s first “associate member,” describing closer ties with Europe as a positive development for the country.

The proposal comes as Canada seeks to strengthen its international economic partnerships amid ongoing trade tensions with the United States, BBC reports.

Speaking after an address to the European Parliament, Carney said a closer alliance with the EU could make Canada a “more effective partner” of the United States.

He also emphasized that deeper ties with Europe would not undermine Canada’s independence, saying Canadians would continue to determine their own language, culture and international agreements.

The proposal is being closely watched in Canada as the government considers whether stronger economic cooperation with Europe can help build greater resilience and expand opportunities for Canadian businesses.

The potential arrangement would represent a new form of relationship between Canada and the EU, although details about what associate membership would entail have yet to be finalized.

World.title: Belize and Poland explore new areas for stronger bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Belize and Poland explore new areas for stronger bilateral cooperation

By Zoila Palma: Today, Francis Fonseca, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, held a bilateral meeting with Jolanta Janek, Ambassador of the Republic of Poland.

Discussions focused on strengthening Belize-Poland relations and advancing cooperation in areas of shared interest, including trade, education, culture, sustainable development and multilateral affairs.

Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to deepening the relationship between Belize and Poland.

World.title: Bouncing back fast
World.content:
WILLIAMS...I see quarters that are becoming less negative and that is a good sign.

CITING data that shows Jamaica 18 months ahead of schedule in recovering from the destruction Hurricane Melissa unleashed on several parishes last year, Finance Minister Fayval Williams on Wednesday painted a rosy picture of the country’s economy. She acknowledged, however, that “not everybody is feeling it just yet”, a nod to critics who have argued that the pace of the recovery and rebuilding is much too slow.

During her upbeat PowerPoint presentation at Wednesday’s post-Cabinet news briefing the minister reeled off data to support her claims.

“When I look at this chart, I see quarters that are becoming less negative and that is a good sign,” Williams stated.

“And, no, this is not a picture of a recession. The Planning Institute of Jamaica (PIOJ) already debunked that notion,” she added.

Williams highlighted that in the quarter following the hurricane, the economy contracted 7.1 per cent, then 4.1 per cent in the next quarter and just 2.9 per cent in the quarter, after that. She said the 2.9 per cent projection should be finalised by the Statistical Institute of Jamaica (Statin) by the end of September.

The finance minister argued that the shrinking year-on-year numbers are themselves proof that the economy is recovering. She argued further that “an economy in decline produces deepening figures, not improving ones”.

Williams urged Jamaicans to remember that immediately after the hurricane, PIOJ projected that the country would not get back to its pre-Melissa level of output until the last quarter of 2028. She noted that the PIOJ now expects that the economy will begin to see growth by the second quarter of 2027 — “six quarters earlier, a year-and-a-half earlier”. According to her, the PIOJ “has been able to revise their forecast because the out-turn keeps getting better”.

The finance minister highlighted that where it was projected that the fiscal deficit would have been 3.8 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP) immediately after the hurricane, it instead came in at 2.5 per cent. At the same time the primary surplus was projected to be 1.3 per cent but came in at 2.3 per cent, while public debt-to-GDP was projected to rise to 68.9 per cent but came in at 65.6 per cent.

Regarding the public debt-to-GDP number, Williams said, “That number matters, it is not a one-off, it’s because we had stronger nominal GDP, the economy itself is bigger than we assumed, and that is the kind of improvement that will persist.”

She also pointed to the positions taken by the big three international ratings agencies with Moody’s upgrading its assessment of Jamaica just seven weeks after the hurricane, which it described as a “temporary setback”. Standard & Poor’s held its rating for Jamaica in December 2025 and moved the outlook to stable, while Fitch affirmed its BB-rating for Jamaica in February 2026 with a stable outlook.

Williams also pointed out that while unemployment rose from 3.3 per cent to 3.7 per cent following the hurricane, it remained at record lows. She acknowledged that unemployment in the hardest-hit parishes was higher.

“I want to assure them that the Government continues to work night and day to restore the west — to restore roads, water, housing, all the services, employment, schools and so on,” she said.

Williams also noted that the response from the Diaspora helped to stabilise the economy, as is evidenced in the record level of remittances that were sent to Jamaica in the aftermath of the hurricane. A breakdown of the numbers shows that, in November, the Diaspora sent remittances totalling US$273 million, up 16 per cent. December saw a record US$296 million being sent. The figure was up 16.3 per cent for the month. Of note is that all of the hardest-hit parishes received more in remittances than before the hurricane.

In the first three months after the storm, Jamaicans abroad sent home US$93 million more than they sent in the same three months a year earlier.

On the matter of inflation, the finance minister insisted that, while it was expected that food prices “would run away” following the devastating hurricane, they did not. She pointed out that inflation moved to 2.9 per cent in October 2025, 4.4 per cent in November 2025, and 4.5 per cent in December 2025 — all within the target range for the Bank of Jamaica. This, she said, was because agricultural production recovered faster than expected.

“Because of that, the price shock was contained,” the minister remarked.

However, Williams acknowledged that by July 2026 the picture had changed completely, with headline inflation surging to 7.5 per cent — the driver being the transportation division, which was up 13.6 per cent. She said based on figures released by Statin on Tuesday, whereas transportation had pushed up inflation in July, it was higher food prices, as a result of the ongoing drought, which drove inflation in August.

While transportation is still a factor, the finance minister said the August inflation number is directly attributable to the upheaval in international markets, driven by the United States war on Iran which has pushed up oil prices since February.

World.title: Blessing in disguise
World.content:
Sharon Logan, director of sales and marketing at Half Moon Resort, speaks during a JAPEX partner media update on Tuesday. (Photo: Aceion Cunningham)

WHEN Hurricane Melissa swept through Jamaica last October it left tourism businesses counting losses and racing to recover. But nearly a year later, Half Moon resort and Chukka Jamaica are looking beyond the devastation, using the disruption to refresh their properties, redesign experiences, and rethink their operations.

For Half Moon, the forced recovery has gone beyond repairing hurricane damage. The Montego Bay resort has used the interruption to undertake a broad refresh of its property, while Chukka Jamaica says the experience forced it to examine its processes and find ways to operate more efficiently.

Speaking during a Jamaica Product Exchange (JAPEX) 2026 Partner Media Update on Tuesday, director of sales and marketing for the Half Moon resort Sharon Logan said the hurricane created an opportunity for the resort to undertake work that would otherwise have been difficult to complete while guests were on property.

“One of the things that I look on is the silver lining behind the cloud, which is that we got the opportunity to do a complete refresh and regrowth of the property since the reopening,” said Logan.

She explained that while some projects, including renovation work on some of the resort’s villas, had already been under way before the hurricane, other major improvements came directly out of the damage caused by the storm.

“The villas were already a project that we were working on. But the other parts of the property, like the original part of the hotel, that has a complete refresh and that is all as a result of the hurricane,” added Logan.

The result, she said, has included improvements across much of the 400-acre property, including its rooms, meeting spaces, lobby, roadways, and pool areas.

One of the more unusual benefits, she identified, came from the movement of sand during the hurricane.

“There are so many open spaces. All the plants have been sprung up fresh and nice…We even got new beaches because we got sand that washed up. That would have cost the hotel millions of dollars to purchase. We got 30 truckloads of sand, free, so we have expanded beaches, so we’re excited about that,” explained Logan.

The resort, which reopened on April 2, is continuing a phased reopening of its facilities. Logan said half of the original Founders’ Cove section is already open, with the remaining section scheduled to open on October 1.

The hurricane also gave the resort an opportunity to tackle work that had previously required interruptions to operations. Logan pointed specifically to the pool at the Eclipse section, which had experienced problems with its tiles.

But while Half Moon’s gains have been visible in its physical transformation, Chukka Jamaica’s experience has produced a different kind of reset.

The attraction operator, which describes itself as a nature adventure company, was particularly exposed to the effects of the hurricane because its business depends heavily on the natural environment.

Group Digital Platform Manager Ilia Tomlinson said the recovery was especially difficult at Chukka’s river locations. At Good Hope in Trelawny, for example, the site was inundated and its river operations were disrupted.

Chukka began reopening locations in November, according to Tomlinson, with its final reopening taking place in June. She said the river-based operations were among the hardest to restore because of the overflow of the waterways.

But the disruption also prompted the company to scrutinise how it worked, with greater productivity emerging as one of the main lessons from the recovery.

“I would say the silver lining is…we operated a little bit more efficiently. We have had to. Nobody wants to cut back, it’s hard decisions to make, but cutting back and being efficient almost go hand in hand where there’s a middle spot where it’s productivity,” said Tomlinson.

“We have had to look at things we have never thought we have had to look at, and in a way we’re thankful for that. You know, it really has had us reflecting on our own processes and procedures and being more efficient in how we deliver our experiences,” added Tomlinson.

That reassessment has taken place alongside changes to Chukka’s tourism products.

In Ocho Rios, the company has redesigned parts of its offering following the hurricane and has expanded its portfolio through its acquisition of the Green Grotto Caves, which it took over just two days before Melissa struck Jamaica on October 28.

The caves, located near Discovery Bay in St Ann, are being incorporated into Chukka’s wider network of experiences in the resort area, adding a stronger history and culture component to its nature and adventure products.

Meanwhile, at Good Hope, the company has rebranded the attraction as a river outpost reflecting its location and the experiences offered there, including river tubing, bamboo rafting, ziplining, and dune buggies.

Tomlinson said the storm also reinforced the importance of preparation, particularly for a company whose operations are so closely tied to Jamaica’s landscape.

“We didn’t know we were so good at preparing. That was the lesson learned on the value of our standards of procedures and policies that we put into place that we probably otherwise take for granted,” she added.

World.title: J-House Vol 1 puts Jamaica on a new global dance floor
World.content:
Freddy Browne

There are collaborations, there are compilations — and then there are projects whose star-studded line-ups pack such a heavy punch that they position themselves for global attention long before anyone hears a single track.

Keen on taking Jamaican voices into the billion-dollar world of electronic music, Freddy Browne’s ambitious J-House Volume 1 is poised to do just that.

With Patra, Beenie Man, Tessanne Chin, Busy Signal, T.O.K, Agent Sasco, and more in the mix, the project, set for release on September 18, aims to take unmistakably Jamaican voices and personalities into the international house music arena.

Rather than simply placing Jamaican artistes over electronic beats and calling it fusion, Browne has been building J-House as its own musical proposition.

According to the American producer, DJ, and JHouse Entertainment CEO, the project stretches across generations of Jamaican music while refusing to stay comfortably inside any one of them.

Each artiste represents a different era in Jamaica’s rich musical history. Patra carries the weight of an artiste who helped push dancehall into mainstream international spaces during the 1990s. Beenie Man has spent decades as one of the genre’s most recognisable figures, while Busy Signal has built a catalogue around his ability to move between hard-core dancehall and broader musical territory. Ding Dong, meanwhile, brings an energy rooted heavily in dance and movement.

Then there is Tessanne Chin, whose victory on The Voice introduced her powerhouse vocals to millions internationally. T.O.K, whose harmonies became integral to dancehall’s crossover era; Richie Stephens, bringing decades of reggae experience; and Agent Sasco, one of the genre’s most respected lyricists.

Newer voices J’Calm and AcYn ensure the project is not only honouring Jamaica’s musical legacy, but also looking towards its future.

Browne, who has previously spoken about imagining artistes such as Ding Dong performing before audiences at major electronic music festivals, described J-House as an opportunity to carry Jamaican talent into spaces it may not traditionally occupy.

“This is crazy,” he said. “We’re creating a blueprint for other producers and record companies. The goal is to open doors for artistes, producers, and the industry as a whole.”

That ambition extends beyond the music itself. House music connects artistes to a vast international network of DJs, clubs, festivals, streaming platforms, radio, play lists, licensing opportunities, and electronic music audiences. J-House is designed to place Jamaican talent directly within that ecosystem, making the project as much about market expansion as it is about musical experimentation.

With J-House Volume 1 distributed through The Orchard/Sony Music the project also has access to an established international distribution network. And Volume 1 is not being treated as the endgame.

Browne shared that Jamaica represents the first instalment of a wider international concept. The United Kingdom is planned as the focus of the second volume, Japan the third, with Africa completing the four-part series. If the vision unfolds as planned, Jamaica will not simply be participating in another global musical movement. It will be the starting point.

World.title: Jamaica, US finalise operating procedures related to TCNs
World.content:
Minister of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade Senator Kamina Johnson Smith confirmed that the United States and Jamaica have finalised operating procedures related to the memorandum of understanding for TCNs that was signed earlier this year..

JAMAICA could soon receive its first batch of third-country nationals (TCNs) from the United States (US) as Foreign Affairs Minister Senator Kamina Johnson Smith confirmed that both governments have finalised operating procedures related to the memorandum of understanding (MOU) that was signed earlier this year.

Jamaica now joins 30 countries, including several members of the Caribbean Community (Caricom), which have similar arrangements with the US Government amid its ongoing crackdown on illegal immigration.

“After internal consultations and thoughtful negotiations, both governments have now finalised operating procedures related to the MOU in order to settle the guard rails and parameters underpinning the agreement. The arrangements were also finalised, taking into account Jamaica’s capacity constraints and our belief in the principles of safe, orderly, and lawful migration,” said Johnson Smith, speaking at a post-Cabinet press briefing at Jamaica House on Wednesday.

The agreement, Johnson Smith clarified, will see 25 TCNs entering the country biweekly. While here, the International Organization for Migration (IOM) will provide basic services, like health care and counselling, to help with their transition.

The minister reiterated that under no circumstance will more than 25 TCNs be present in the island.

“We have also not agreed to receive 10,000 individuals. We have negotiated guard rails to address capacity constraints, and have, therefore, agreed to a maximum of 25 individuals per two-week period, which the IOM will, of course, be on a continuous basis making arrangements for their return.

“Furthermore, this arrangement will be suspended if 10 TCNs apply to remain in Jamaica through asylum procedures or other humanitarian applications. This, again, is specifically negotiated by Jamaica,” said Johnson Smith.

She further explained that TCNs were not deportees but the nationals of other countries who entered the US unlawfully and are being returned to their home countries through the IOM’s Assisted Voluntary Return Programme.

Johnson Smith added that while she is aware that some countries have opted to accept TCNs with criminal records, Jamaica will only facilitate those with no previous convictions.

“The Government reiterates its commitment to working with the IOM and the Government of the United States of America to ensure that all arrangements for the next stage of TCN implementation are appropriately governed and implemented in accordance with both our domestic laws and international law,” she said.

Additionally, while acknowledging Minister of National Security Dr Horace Chang’s previous commitment to release the agreement, Johnson Smith explained that the MOU’s bilateral status prevents it from being made public.

“As indicated, this is not a unilateral arrangement; it is a bilateral arrangement, and one in which they [the United States] have not generally released their agreements, and they have not agreed to release this one,” she said.

“I give you every assurance as well that we have all shared all the relevant and material matters, provisions, in relation to the matter. So there’s nothing being hidden per se, but as you would note, even under the ATI [Access to Information Act], bilateral agreements, security agreements, arrangements that are sensitive to relations between countries and otherwise are treated differently from other agreements,” explained Johnson Smith.

Despite not being able to give an official start date for when the first TCNs are expected to arrive, Johnson Smith affirmed that Jamaicans will be regularly updated as conversations advance.

World.title: NEXT LEVEL
World.content:
Jamaica 100m sprinter Jonielle Smith competes in the women’s 4x100m relay heats during the World Athletics Championships in Tokyo, Japan, on September 20, 2025. (Photo: AFP)

After breaking into the ranks of Jamaica’s fastest women ever, national 100m sprinter Jonielle Smith says she’s looking to carry her strong form into next season with the World Athletics Championships looming.

Smith ended her impressive 2026 season over the weekend at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship in Budapest, finishing fourth in the women’s 100m final and helping Jamaica land silver in the 4×100 metres mixed relay.

The 2025 North American, Central American and Caribbean (NACAC) 100m champion moved to 14th all time in Jamaica’s all-time list when she clocked a personal best 10.89 seconds at the Eugene Diamond League in July.

Prior to this year, Smith had never gone under 11 seconds in the event. However, she managed to dip under the mark six times, including at the Ultimate Championship where she registered 10.94 seconds both in the semi-final and final.

Smith, a finalist at this summer’s Commonwealth Games in Scotland and March’s World Indoor Championships in Poland, believes improving her confidence level was key in her success this year.

“I’m proud of myself [for] having confidence in myself,” she told the Inside Lane UK. “As good as last year was, it took me a while to start to trust my body and I feel like from day one this year in the background, I told myself that I was a champion and I was going to get what I wanted done and I think that’s what I’m most proud of, just being confident.”

The 30-year-old, who won 4x100m silver at last year’s Tokyo World Championships, says writing out her goals has helped change her perspective, which was on display at the recent Ultimate Championship.

“I journalled every day before practice and I had to do that [for the 100m final] also,” she said. “After the 4x100m, I felt bad because I really wanted us to win and I wasn’t able to pass [USA’s] Kayla [White]. She’s a phenomenal athlete, but I wanted us to win [0:44] to be honest, so I genuinely felt bad. My people were like ‘you split nine [seconds], that was so good’. But regardless, it was just like we didn’t win.

“So I went back to what I was used to and I journalled, I told myself that I’m a champion and I reminded myself what we were doing, trying to have fun and stuff like that. And I felt like that made me come out a whole lot more confident since the last month and the results showed.”

Describing 2026 as “phenomenal”, Smith says she’s excited for what’s to come in 2027.

“I got my 10.8, I got top three at the national trials and Ultimate finalist,” she said. “I just didn’t get [a] Commonwealth [medal] but that was out of my control, so I got to give myself some grace for that. But I feel like I finished off extremely well and I started even better indoors, so it’s a great thing to build off going into next season.”

Smith will likely be eyeing an individual spot at the 2027 World Championships in Beijing, having last done so in 2019 in Doha.

World.title: Shan’s Garlic, Thyme & Scotch Bonnet Butter Ribeye
World.content:
Shanice Gore completes the spread, serving up the garlic, thyme, and Scotch bonnet butter ribeye. (Photo: Alan Smith)

Get ready for a flavour-packed feast Mia Hair Artistry principal Shanice Gore shares her Garlic, Thyme & Scotch Bonnet Butter Ribeye recipe with Thursday Food.

“Ribeye is one of my favourite cuts of steak because of its beautiful marbling and rich flavour. In my home, we love our steak cooked medium rare, so I focus on getting a good, flavourful sear on the outside while keeping the centre juicy and tender. My garlic, thyme and Scotch bonnet compound butter is the finishing touch — it melts beautifully over the hot steak and adds a delicious Jamaican kick,” says Gore.

Ingredients

•1 ribeye steak, approximately 1–1½ inches thick

• Salt, to taste

• Freshly cracked black pepper, to taste

• 1 tablespoon olive oil

For the Compound Butter:

• ½ cup unsalted butter, softened

• 2 cloves garlic, finely minced

• 1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves

• ½–1 Scotch bonnet pepper, finely minced, depending on desired heat

Method

1. Begin by preparing the compound butter. Combine the softened butter with the garlic, thyme and finely minced Scotch bonnet pepper. Mix well until everything is evenly incorporated. Place the butter onto parchment paper, shape into a log, roll tightly and refrigerate until firm.

2. Remove the ribeye from the refrigerator about 30 minutes before cooking and pat dry with paper towels. Season both sides generously with salt and freshly cracked black pepper.

3. Heat a heavy skillet or cast-iron pan over high heat until very hot. Add the olive oil and carefully place the steak into the pan. Sear undisturbed until a deep golden-brown crust forms, then flip and sear the other side.

4. For a ribeye approximately 1–1½ inches thick, cook for approximately three to four minutes per side for medium rare, four to five minutes per side for medium, or six to seven minutes per side for well done. Cooking times will vary depending on the thickness of the steak, so a meat thermometer can be used for accuracy.

5. Once the steak has been seared on both sides, reduce the heat or remove the pan from the heat and place a generous spoonful of the garlic, thyme and Scotch bonnet compound butter directly on top of the steak. Allow butter to melt over the hot meat, spooning the melted butter over the steak.

6. Remove the ribeye from the pan and leave it to rest for five to 10 minutes before slicing. Slice against the grain and serve with the melted compound butter spooned over the top.

Shan’s Tip: For the juiciest ribeye, don’t skip the resting time. And in my home, medium rare is the preferred doneness — the combination of the tender, juicy steak and the spicy, garlicky compound butter is hard to beat.

World.title: Family services shake-up
World.content:
The Ministry of Education has severed ties with the heads of two of its primary family services agencies — the Child Protection and Family Services Agency (CPFSA) and the National Parenting Support Commission (NPSC) — reportedly to undertake a major shift in their operations, the Jamaica Observer has learnt.

As part of that shake-up, chief executive officer of the CPFSA Laurette Adams-Thomas, who took the helm of the agency in October 2023, will demit office next month.

In a brief response to the Observer, Adams-Thomas said her contract expires on October 1, 2026 and she was “officially notified on July 23, 2026” that it would “not be renewed”.

The CPFSA is an executive agency which was formed from the merger of the Child Development Agency (CDA) and the Office of Children’s Registry (OCR). Adams-Thomas, an educator and social worker, took over its leadership following an eight-year stint as general manager of the largest infirmary in the Caribbean — Jamaica’s Golden Age Home — where she had oversight responsibly for protection and welfare services for more than 450 indigent people from the parishes of Kingston and St Andrew. Prior to assuming that position, she was interim executive director/registrar at the OCR, where her focus was centred on ensuring that an effective system was maintained to facilitate the confidential receipt, assessment, and referral of reports of known or suspected cases of child abuse.

She holds a master’s degree in business administration, bachelor of science in human resource management, and a number of certifications in leadership, corporate governance and strategic planning.

In the meantime, the Observer was reliably informed on Monday that NPSC CEO Kaysia Kerr “is no longer with” the entity. Efforts to get an official response from Kerr were unsuccessful. A pre-recorded message on her personal mobile phone directed all callers with queries related to the commission to contact the education ministry or the commission itself.

A source with knowledge of the development said the ministry had decided to disengage with Kerr due to a breakdown in relations.

She took the helm of the commission in 2017, succeeding Dr Patrece Charles. In an interview with the

Observer at the time, Kerr said she hoped to craft and design programmes for parents and children of all 13 categories of disabilities, move the organisation out of eastern Jamaica to serve other parishes, take some of the programmes internationally, and get the unit to a stage where it generates income.

The former NPSC head has a solid background in education and has completed studies in business and professional management at Nova Southeastern University, along with a first degree in special education and a master’s in administration and supervision from Western Carolina University.

The commission coordinates a wide range of services for parents and also delivers programmes that build parenting skills and promote parental involvement in education.

The Government of Jamaica mandated the establishment of the NPSC in response to the 2004 task force report on the status of education in Jamaica.

The NPSC began operating in January 2013.

World.title: Global aviation squeeze
World.content:
Jamaica Tourist Board (JTB) Deputy Director of Tourism for the Americas Philip Rose says Jamaica needs more airline seats to meet strong demand as carriers face aircraft shortages and higher fuel costs amid the impact of the war in the Middle East.

Addressing the media during the Jamaica Product Exchange (JAPEX) forum in Ocho Rios on Tuesday, Rose said Jamaica’s immediate challenge is not a lack of demand, but having enough airline seats to bring visitors to the island.

“The immediate thing that we do need is more seats into the destination. The good news is, and I really want this to land, the good news is the airlines know this. The airlines are preparing because they don’t want to leave business on the table. The airlines know that the demand is there. The airlines are preparing to put in additional flights,” he said.

His comments come as Jamaica’s tourism industry continues its recovery following last year’s Hurricane Melissa, with hotel capacity gradually returning and airlines looking to adjust their schedules accordingly.

Rose said the global aviation industry is itself under pressure, making it difficult for airlines to simply add capacity whenever demand rises. He pointed to higher fuel costs linked to developments in the Middle East, as well as problems affecting aircraft engines, servicing and maintenance.

“As you all know, there are global pressures now on the aviation space. What’s happening out there in the Middle East has really impacted oil prices, which impacts fuel prices. In the best of days, the margins are exceedingly thin for airlines. You’re going to add this increase in jet fuel, it puts additional pressure on the industry,” he explained.

“Along with that, there is a shortage of aircraft because of issues to do with the engines, which I won’t really bore you all with. There are some service and maintenance things that are going on, which means a lot of aircraft have been pulled out of service,” he added.

The result, he said, is that Jamaica cannot depend on unlimited airline capacity, even as demand remains strong

“Airlines across the world don’t have infinite aircraft. That means that seats are not infinite. When the seats are full, the seats are full. Because of the demand that we have been generating for Jamaica, the vast majority of the flights into Jamaica are full,” he added.

Still, Rose said the outlook for airlift is positive, with airlines preparing to increase service as more hotel rooms become available.

He said airlines are also preparing to return to the flight schedules that existed before Hurricane Melissa, although they first have to resolve their own aircraft availability issues and factor in Jamaica’s accommodation capacity.

World.title: Tusk warns of ‘accidental’ Russian strikes against Ukraine’s allies in fall and winter
World.content:
Under NATO’s Article 5, an armed attack on one member is viewed as an attack on all. Russian hybrid attacks, espionage and stray drones have probed the threshold of what constitutes an armed attack.

“There is a real risk that drones or other types of missiles could enter the territory of one or several NATO countries on the eastern flank and cause damage. And the official narrative will be that it was an accident and that there is no reason for anyone to consider any kind of NATO response,” Tusk said.

He also said that “not all politicians in the West, in the United States or Europe are thinking about how to defend Poland, Lithuania, Latvia or Estonia, dreaming of immediately proving that they are ironclad allies and will come to Poland’s aid under Article 5.”

“You know that yourselves,” Tusk added.

U.S. President Donald Trump has on numerous occasions cast doubt on the principle of collective defense.

The prime minister also said that some politicians and political groups in Europe were “just waiting for an excuse” to declare, in the event of a conflict, that “we are not going to die for Poland, we are not going to die for Latvia or Lithuania.”

The warning came as Tusk said the coming fall and winter months could prove “tragically critical” for Ukraine, with Russia expected to carry out continuous, high-intensity strikes on major Ukrainian cities while targeting warehouses, rail infrastructure and other logistics essential to the country’s defense.

Such attacks have intensified in recent weeks, also covering western Ukraine close to the Polish border, as Russia has increased its use of jet-powered drones that Ukraine has struggled to intercept.

World.title: AI king Jensen Huang pushes ‘responsible optimism’ at King Charles III’s gathering
World.content:
For the first time since worries about AI eradicating humanity sparked a wave of calls for immediate regulation, the companies were all under one roof. Charles addressed the dire warnings in his remarks to his guests.

“There seems urgency in adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands and being used in potentially catastrophic ways,” he said. “Surely, then, we need sufficient means of control before it is all too late.”

But after weeks of fervent debate about the need to increase oversight and slow the pace of development, tech leaders at the event were eager to change the mood music back to something sunnier.

Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia, whose chips are the engines for almost every player in the AI race, said “we have to build this technology safely and securely and responsibly” — but also with what he termed “responsible optimism.”

And while “every government should be involved,” Huang argued against sweeping new laws, saying the onus was primarily on the industry to ensure its products are safe.

“Those of us building AI must test systems rigorously, protect privacy, anticipate misuse, and secure the infrastructure society will depend on. When a product is not safe enough, we should hold it back and keep engineering,” he said — a thinly veiled rebuke to leading AI labs such as OpenAI and Anthropic whose agents sparked the most recent panic, and whose representatives were in the room.

World.title: Romanian president taps EU lawmaker Mureșan to lead country out of crisis
World.content:
Shortly after the announcement, Mureșan wrote on social media that he accepted the president’s proposal, adding that “Romania needs a credible government as soon as possible.”

Romania has been in political crisis since April, when the Social Democratic Party teamed up with the far-right Alliance for the Union of Romanians to topple then-Prime Minister Ilie Bolojan over his austerity policies.

Dan’s first two nominees for Bolojan’s replacement failed to secure enough party support to lead a new administration.

Mureșan now has ten days to form a cabinet and win a vote of confidence in parliament. He is supported by the National Liberal Party, of which he is a member, as well as the Save Romania Union and the Democratic Alliance of Hungarians in Romania.

But he has received an icy welcome from the Social Democrats and the Alliance — the two largest parties in Romania’s lower chamber — who appear to take issue with Mureșan’s position as an EU lawmaker.

The Social Democrats’ president, former Prime Minister Sorin Grindeanu, said in a Facebook post that he was “surprised and disappointed” by the nomination of “a man who, just days before this nomination, was waging a fierce campaign in Brussels against his own country to cut European funds.”

Also on Facebook, using flag and roses emojis, Alliance leader George Simion wrote: “We are not voting Germany, nor France, nor [the Social Democrats]. Only Romania.”

Mureșan has been part of the European Parliament since 2014, a vice-president of the European People’s Party since 2019, and a leading voice on EU budget talks in the European Parliament. He is a co-rapporteur for the upcoming Multiannual Financial Framework — the bloc’s seven-year budget — for 2028 to 2034.

World.title: Russia’s global fuel customers push back against US sanctions bill
World.content:
Donald Trump has not said whether he will sign the Russia sanctions bill. | Igor Ivanko/AFP via Getty Images

The global response to the Russia sanctions bill the U.S. Congress approved late Wednesday has been swift and defiant, with Moscow warning it would prolong its war on Ukraine, India vowing to protect its interests, and Beijing pushing back against what it called illegal “long-arm jurisdiction.”

The bill, which U.S. President Donald Trump must still sign into law, would slap mandatory sanctions on Moscow’s leadership, energy sector, defense industry and “shadow fleet” seaborne delivery system for embargoed Russian fuel.

It also empowers Trump to hit the five largest global purchasers of that fuel with 100% sanctions, a cudgel that has U.S. allies worried. China has bought 50% of Russian crude exports since 2022, India 37%, Turkey 5% — and the EU 5%. The bloc has also been the largest buyer of Russian LNG (49%) over that period, as well as the largest buyer of Russian pipeline gas (32%), according to data from the Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air non-profit.

World.title: French presidential hopeful Attal vows to build ‘United States of Europe’
World.content:
To better compete with the U.S. and China, Attal proposed implementing a two-speed EU so like-minded partners can more quickly merge their economies, regulatory frameworks and labor and capital via a new dedicated treaty to be approved by citizens via referendum. Attal also advocated for joint European debt, removing intra-bloc trade barriers and encouraging bloc-wide mergers, especially in telecoms and financial services.

Attal’s advisers told reporters that the former prime minister is trying to stake out a position as one of the most pro-European options in a crowded field of candidates. The 37-year-old centrist has struggled to break through, and polls have repeatedly shown him lagging behind his main ideological rival, Edouard Philippe, and euroskeptic front-runner Marine Le Pen.

But since launching his campaign in May, Philippe has stayed relatively quiet on matters relating to Brussels — which gives Attal a way to better distinguish his campaign from that of Philippe.

It’s a risky strategy, though. Voters in France are less sanguine about the bloc’s future than other Europeans, with many still frustrated after the Commission last year pushed through a massive trade deal with Latin America that was widely viewed domestically as a threat to the French agriculture industry. The EU is also seen as a source of environmental rules that French farmers consider too strict while business see the bloc as a source of red tape.

Attal in his speech paid tribute to Macron’s European legacy while also criticizing European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, accusing her of overlooking the bloc’s problems in her Wednesday State of the Union speech — which he called “too little, too late.” He also hit out against the trade deal she agreed to with U.S. President Donald Trump last year.

Should Attal win, it will be up to von der Leyen to decide the professional fate of his romantic partner, Industry Commissioner Stéphane Séjourné, given the potential conflict of interest. Séjourné swore an oath upon taking office to prioritize EU interests over national matters, and his term runs beyond the French presidential election in April 2027.

World.title: French PM to propose €54B budget squeeze for 2027
World.content:
France has in recent years struggled to rein in spending and a debt burden that has grown from €2.3 trillion to more than €3.5 trillion and is becoming increasingly expensive to service as interest rates spike across the world. Lecornu, who vigorously opposes tax hikes on any segments of the population, said the country needs to find an additional €10 billion to finance the debt.

“The debt burden is weighing increasingly heavily on the budget equation,” he said.

Lecornu said the 2027 budget deficit target was 5%, while the hope is to contain this year’s deficit to less than 5.5%

The French government had initially planned on reducing its deficit to 4.7% of GDP this year — but acknowledged last week that the figure would ultimately land above 5%. It also cut its growth forecast for this year and next year to 0.5% in 2026 and 1% in 2027.

The government targeted €30 billion in the 2026 budget and €60 billion the year prior.

Lecornu’s minority government will present its budget bill to lawmakers in the coming weeks, but getting it passed will be difficult without a governing majority and as the spring 2027 presidential election gets closer, which will incentivize parties to stake out their positions ahead of an electoral cycle.

World.title: Greek parliament lifts Avramopoulos immunity for Brussels corruption probe
World.content:
The Greek parliament on Thursday voted to lift the parliamentary immunity of former European Commissioner Dimitris Avramopoulos, clearing the way for Belgian authorities to continue their actions in the investigation into the affair known as Qatargate.

 

Of the 266 MPs present, 264 voted in favour of lifting his immunity, while two declared themselves "present". The parliament's Ethics Committee had earlier unanimously recommended the move. The procedure followed the issuing of a European arrest warrant by a Belgian investigating judge in June.

The 73-year-old Dimitris Avramopoulos, an MP for the ruling New Democracy party, served as European Commissioner for Migration from 2014 to 2019 and previously as mayor of Athens. He has categorically denied any illegal activity.

He had himself requested the lifting of his immunity, stating in a memorandum to parliament that he wished to cooperate fully with the competent authorities.

"I have never participated, directly or indirectly, in any illegal activity and I have never acted to serve the unlawful interests of any state or third party," he said.

He added that he is not seeking protection from the investigation, but the opportunity "to present the factual evidence" and to prove that he has no connection with the acts under scrutiny.

Relationship with the NGO Fight Impunity

The Belgian investigation concerns, among other things, Dimitris Avramopoulos's links with the non-governmental organisation Fight Impunity, founded by former Italian MEP Antonio Panzeri, one of the central figures in the case.

Dimitris Avramopoulos sat on the organisation's honorary board in 2020-2021, after the end of his term at the European Commission.

He has maintained that his cooperation with Fight Impunity was entirely lawful and that the related fees were declared to the tax authorities.

"My involvement in the organisation Fight Impunity was entirely lawful, vetted, approved, declared and taxed," he said when the warrant became public in June.

The European arrest warrant relates to allegations of participation in a criminal organisation, public corruption and the laundering of proceeds from illegal activities, according to a document from the Greek authorities cited by international news agencies.

The charges remain the subject of the Belgian investigation and do not constitute a guilty finding.

The long story of the Belgian authorities' investigation

The probe began in December 2022, when Belgian authorities carried out a series of searches and arrests over allegations that foreign governments sought to influence decisions in the European Parliament through money and gifts.

In the course of the case, Belgian authorities have seized around 1.5 million euros in cash. Those arrested included former Italian MEP Antonio Panzeri and the then vice-president of the European Parliament, Eva Kaili.

Qatar and Morocco have been accused of trying to sway European decisions and improve on their public image. Both countries have denied the allegations.

The Belgian investigation has been significantly delayed because of legal appeals challenging the lawfulness of certain procedural steps.

World.title: Tusk: intelligence sees Russian plan for drone strikes on Poland, allies
World.content:
Prime Minister Donald Tusk, in a special address to the Sejm, said he was presenting the public and MPs with "the most probable scenario for the coming few months".

 

"It is a scenario involving serious events and requiring us to be focused, serious and, above all, mentally ready to pass difficult tests," Tusk said.

He stressed that such tests "certainly lie ahead for all Poles".

The head of government pointed out that his comments refer to the period up to early spring, "because, according to all sources, it is late autumn and winter that will be the most critical phase of the Russian-Ukrainian war so far".

Jet-powered drones: Russia's new weapon

He also pointed to a significant development "of a very negative nature": Russia is rolling out on a mass scale a new type of drone – jet-powered drones that travel at much higher speeds and operate at high altitude before dropping and hitting their target. He noted that hardly anyone is effectively prepared to counter them and that "this is work we, too, have to do".

Tusk announced he would travel to Ukraine to talk with President Volodymyr Zelensky "about how we can cooperate within the anti-ballistic coalition and make use of the skills, capabilities and capacities of Ukraine and other countries in this field as well".

He also referred to the unfulfilled promises of an energy truce previously mentioned by US President Donald Trump.

"Since then, there have been many attacks, including on energy infrastructure in Ukraine. We must therefore assume this will continue, which also has consequences for Poland, as these attacks are increasingly targeting installations very close to our border crossings with Ukraine," he said.

According to the prime minister, Russia's aim is to destroy Ukraine's economy and logistics on as large a scale as possible. "For now, Ukraine's," he added pointedly.

Tough exams lie ahead of us. Anyone who questions our alliances today harms Poland. We must be prepared for every scenario.

Six main Ukrainian cities in Russia's sights

The Polish prime minister said constant strikes of very high frequency and intensity are expected on six key Ukrainian cities, along with the destruction of stockpiles of supplies essential for the country's defence and of railway infrastructure. Tusk recalled that in the past several weeks Russians have destroyed more than 300 Ukrainian railway locomotives.

The head of government said that "in the assessment of intelligence services, Russia's plans also include hybrid strikes with drones and missiles on states supporting Ukraine, including Poland". Such possibilities have been mentioned for some time, but now, Tusk stressed, the information is already "highly consistent and, unfortunately, persuasive".

In the prime minister's view, potential strikes will be "so-called 'accidental'", aimed at paralysing or weakening NATO members' motivation to invoke alliance provisions in the event of aggression.

"There is a real risk that the territory of one or several NATO countries on the eastern flank may be entered by drones or other types of missiles, which may even cause destruction. And the official narrative will be that this is an accident and that there is no reason for anyone to contemplate any response from NATO," he said.

Russia's objective, he said, is "to weaken NATO's overall cohesion and, above all, to convince NATO countries that Article 5 is more theoretical than practical". Such "accidental" strikes may be repeated.

Tusk: on security, we must speak with one voice

Continuing, the prime minister said that Russia's new strategy also envisages possible political changes in some European countries. He recalled the forthcoming elections and the presence of forces that can be described as an openly pro-Russian option. He appealed to politicians, regardless of party colours – addressing in particular MPs from the Confederation party – "under no circumstances to take part, whether inadvertently or deliberately, in promoting narratives that Russia cares deeply about".

"Whipping up hostility towards the European Union, towards our allies, towards Ukrainians, is directly implementing Russia's strategy. Everyone must finally understand this," he underlined.

In closing, Tusk called on everyone present in the Sejm chamber to "speak with one voice, take joint decisions, hesitate no longer and show that, regardless of political views, we are all patriots in a moment of trial" when it comes to the security of borders, Polish airspace and people's homes. He pointed out that some politicians in Europe "are just waiting for an alibi" so that, in the event of conflict, they can argue: "We will not die for Poland, we will not perish for Latvia or Lithuania".

"Article 5, allied loyalty, fidelity to commitments must become our hallmark," he declared. He added that Poland wants and needs certainty that, in the event of a more serious threat from Russia, it can "count on a swift and effective response from the entire bloc".

World.title: King Charles urges tech bosses to keep AI under human control
World.content:
Britain's King Charles III has met with senior AI figures where he urged them to keep artificial intelligence technologies under human control and ensure it serves people, communities and the environment.

 

Representatives from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind and Nvidia were hosted by the King at Dumfries House in Scotland to discuss how AI can benefit society while limiting its risks.

Joining the King and AI bosses, including the CEO of AI giant Nvidia Jensen Huang, was the UK's newly appointed Minister for Artificial Intelligence, Kanishka Narayan.

In his opening remarks, the King referenced the rapid speed at which AI has come: "The development of AI – its substance and its pace – are both intriguing and deeply concerning in equal measure,"

The "existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways” should be urgently considered, he added.

King Charles gives a speech during a meeting for leaders from the artificial intelligence sector. Thursday 17 September Jonathan Brady/PA via AP, Pool

In his speech, King Charles did not name any countries or companies, but said he wanted those in the room to find ways to use AI for beneficial purposes “with safety at its heart” and consider how to “build international cooperation and consensus” to achieve that.

Concerns about the future of AI

The meeting in Scotland comes after several high profile incidents regarding the safety of AI technology.

Last week Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon made headlines by resigning and publishing a serious warning about the technology's potential risks. Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei responded with an essay saying that the industry might need to slow the pace of its work.

On Wednesday OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, reported six incidents of “unexpected or concerning” behaviour by its models. These include performing tasks without authorisation, coordinating with other models and evading oversight by human researchers.

Nvidia's Huang, on the other hand, has criticised the call for slowing down. The Nvidia CEO said it should be up to individual companies to develop their AI technology safely and test it properly before releasing any products to the public.

“When a product is not safe enough, we should hold it back and keep engineering. We’ve always done that and we should continue to do that,” he said in his speech following the king's remarks.

World.title: Trump determined to end Iran war soon, US president's senior adviser tells Euronews
World.content:
US President Donald Trump expects the war across the Middle East to end soon and is determined to bring it to a close, his senior adviser on Arab and Middle Eastern affairs Massad Boulos told Euronews.

 

Boulos declined to give a timeline, saying the moment would be Trump's to choose.

"The president believes that it’s going to end soon, and he’s determined to make it end. And he’s working towards that," Boulos told Euronews at the Arab Media Summit in Dubai.

"He’s a person who delivers, and we’ve all seen President Trump deliver on his promises. There’s no promise that he didn’t deliver on, whether it’s a campaign promise or any other promise that he made," he explained.

Pressed on when that would happen, Boulos said, "That will be for the president to determine."

"But we are very hopeful, and we are absolutely solidly behind him and behind his leadership," he added.

Boulos set the nuclear question as the condition that has to be settled before the war stops, repeating that Tehran will not be permitted to acquire a nuclear weapon.

"Somebody had to tackle and had to address this nuclear issue. As President Trump has said repeatedly, there is no way we can allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon," Boulos said.

"Just imagine a world, just imagine this region with a nuclear Iran. Just imagine that for a moment," he added.

"He’s giving negotiations and talks a chance. He’s been extremely patient. And we hope that ultimately peace will prevail."

"He’s firm on that and he’s determined. We are in full support of his vision, and so are his partners in the region. Nobody wants war."

Boulos, who described Trump as "the president of peace", said that Trump had already brought other conflicts to an end and was working on two more.

"We know that he’s the only president, at least in recent history, but definitely in the world, that has solved eight conflicts and eight wars so far. And he’s working on the ninth and the 10th," he said.

"If you look at the Pakistan-India conflict, just talk to them and they will tell you that what President Trump was able to achieve saved them at least probably 4 or 5 million lives."

He gave no detail of which conflicts he was referring to and did not expand further on the casualty figure.

Gulf states Washington's 'true partners'

Boulos said expansion of the Abraham Accords, four of which were signed during Trump’s first term, had been interrupted by the 2020 election and would resume once the current war was resolved.

"If it wasn’t for the re-election campaign, there were many more that were ready, lined up and ready to sign the Abraham Accords," he said.

"We do believe that this should be addressed soon, and then we can go back to our peace initiatives."

Gulf states including the UAE and Qatar have questioned in recent months whether existing arrangements do enough for their security.

Boulos said the relationship with Washington was strong at the leadership and working level, naming Saudi Arabia, Egypt and Jordan alongside them.

"These are true partners. They are true allies. He has an excellent relationship, including a personal relationship with them, and an excellent rapport and chemistry with these leaders," he said.

"There are coordination's happening at all sorts of different levels and departments within our administration. So, I can assure you that it’s working out quite well, just like any good partners."

Asked about public opinion in the region, Boulos, who worked on Trump’s campaign with Christian, Muslim and other communities in the US, said support rested in part on social conservatism.

"I travel all over the Middle East and I meet with Middle Eastern leaders and with the people of the Middle East. They all love President Trump," he said.

"If you look at the social aspect, the values, family values, and those principles that are deeply entrenched in Middle Eastern culture," Boulos explained.

"His campaign was about fighting the woke ideology, and the Middle Eastern communities fully support that."

Humanitarian support for Sudan

Boulos singled out Sudan as the administration’s most pressing humanitarian file, and said the president wanted that war ended quickly as well.

"Sudan today is the world’s biggest humanitarian catastrophe," he said. He put the number of Sudanese people in need of aid at 35 million, of whom he said 25 million were living in famine-like conditions.

He said the US remained the single largest humanitarian contributor there, with more than $3 billion provided since the start of the war.

Washington has provided no support beyond humanitarian aid and diplomatic effort, Boulos said, pointing to an arms embargo the US is pursuing at the UN Security Council.

On domestic politics, Boulos said the US president was campaigning intensively ahead of the midterm elections and had held what he described as the first-ever midterm convention in Dallas, adding that the Iran war was unlikely to directly shape the result.

"There are many domestic issues usually that are predominantly in terms of priority. With the American voter, with the average US voter, there are many other domestic priorities," Boulos concluded.

World.title: UAE presidential adviser Gargash says trust with Iran will take years to rebuild
World.content:
Trust between the United Arab Emirates and Iran will take years to rebuild, UAE president's diplomatic adviser Dr Anwar Gargash said on Thursday.

 

Speaking at the Arab Media Summit in Dubai, he said relations with Tehran had to continue because the two countries were neighbours, but that confidence was a separate question after the attacks on the Gulf states.

Gargash said the UAE was managing the crisis while also assessing the future of the relationship.

“At the end of the day, we are neighbours, geographically neighbours. We have very complex relations with Iran, and certainly there is a collapse in the security regiment in the region. Thus, we have to find some new channels of understanding,” he said.

He set out the UAE approach in three parts. “Our role, or rather our approach, is based on three elements. First, to defend our sovereignty, and then to be flexible,” he said. The third was continuity of economic development through the crisis, he said, citing the president's visit to Germany.

“We have to try. To maintain our development, our economic uproar, and the visit of our president to Germany was successful because we don't want to stop our economy in the midst of this crisis,” he said.

Asked about his 7 September statement that UAE confidence in Iran was broken, Gargash said he had drawn a deliberate distinction.

“Actually, I differentiated between the relations and the trust, and I said that the relations are a must and we should have communication and relations with Iran based on open dialogue and a dialogue that would overcome the daily matters,” he said.

“Confidence building, I believe, will take us a long time. We need years to rebuild this trust.”

“The Iranian president said that the aggression from Iran on the GCC countries was a big mistake,” he said.

“I think it is a geostrategic mistake that created a more complex situation for Iran that would affect its future.”

'UAE is a nice country but not an easy target'

He said Iran's use of proxy militias kept it close to the aggression, and that the Gulf states would be the parties to broker Tehran's return to its international place, trade and commerce, once the attacks stopped.

“They can't negotiate a new future while they are still threatening and being aggressive against the neighbourhood,” he said.

Asked whether the UAE had taken any measures of its own against Iran, financial or political, he said it had not.

“No, we have only defended ourselves, and we continue to defend ourselves, and we still extend our hands for friendly relations”, he said.

Gargash said Iran was made of different circles and that decision-making there was no longer held in one place, as it had been under the previous Ayatollah Ali Khamenei since 1989, and that the voices arguing against confrontation with the Gulf needed to be louder.

On the meeting between Sheikh Khalid bin Mohamed and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian at BRICS, Gargash said the two sides had agreed on the direction if not on everything.

“There was not a complete agreement between them. But there was an agreement on the fact that we should start a new page and look to the future,” he said.

“The future should never be like what we have now. It is not in the interest of Iran nor the GCC countries.”

He said President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed had set the balance between flexibility and strength from the beginning of the war.

“The UAE is a nice country, but we are not an easy target,” Gargash said. “He was so clear in saying that Iran is going to be away from stability for decades to come.”

Houthi control of Bab el-Mandeb 'concern for everyone'

Asked about the drone and rocket fire that triggered alerts in Saudi Arabia's city of Jeddah and Islam's holiest site of Mecca, Gargash said that "targeting Mecca is completely denounced and rejected.”

“The security and the sovereignty of Saudi Arabia is part of our security, and the stability of the GCC countries is interconnected,” he said.

The region had suffered from militias, Gargash said, naming Hezbollah in Lebanon and the Houthis in Yemen, and that “any arms outside the state are harmful for the countries and the region”.

“Yes, the channels are open. And as you are aware, and strategically speaking, the safety, security, and prosperity of Saudi Arabia is in our interest,” he said, asked whether relations with Riyadh remained open.

On the Houthis' offensive to take control of the Bab el-Mandeb strait, Gargash said that "the Houthis' control over the strait is a concern for everyone," and not just a regional issue.

"This is not related to the region, but rather to the international economy," he said. “We go back to the basic principle that these straits are international. This is the international definition."

Gargash set out no timetable for further contacts with Tehran, saying the UAE did not choose the war but defended itself when it started, and that “this is a beginning for a political dialogue that should be started”.

World.title: Trump hails 'major progress' in setting up US base in Poland
World.content:
The location of the permanent US military base in Poland could be announced "very soon," Donald Trump has said. The US president also praised the leadership of his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki.

US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that significant progress had been made toward establishing a US military base in Poland.

"Thanks to the bold leadership of my friend, Karol Nawrocki, President of Poland, major progress is being made toward establishing a US Army base in Poland," Trump said in a post on Truth Social.

In August, Warsaw revealed that it was in talks with Washington regarding a permanent US military presence in Poland.

"If this happens, the location will be announced very soon. This will be a historic step for our Great US/Polish Alliance," Trump added in a social media post.

His announcement comes despite his administration's launch of a formal review of its military presence in Europe. This has raised fears among allies that the US could reduce its military presence there.

How did Warsaw react?

Nawrocki, who is a conservative ally of the US president, thanked Trump on X, saying Poland was "ready to continue our efforts to strengthen our defense cooperation."

He added, "I can assure you that the Polish government will do its utmost to provide the best possible location for the US Army base."

Meanwhile, Zbigniew Bogucki, the head of the Polish president's chancellery, called Trump's announcement "great news for Poland." He also noted that it came on the 87th anniversary of the Soviet invasion of Poland.

In August, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Pawel Zalewski said his country was discussing with the United States the possibility of establishing a permanent US base on its territory.

"We have already completed the initial stage of the process, not to mention the political will, which was expressed long ago," Zalewski told the public broadcaster TVP.

Can Poland hold NATO’s line against Russia without the US? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

Poland secures NATO's eastern flank

Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, Poland has been pushing for a larger allied presence on NATO's eastern flank.

Nearly 10,000 US soldiers are currently stationed in Poland, a member of both NATO and the EU. However, they are there almost exclusively on a rotational basis.

Poland's proximity to Ukraine and Russia is a key factor in its security strategy. The country allocates approximately 5% of its gross domestic product to defense spending and has been working to increase the United States' military presence.

In the meantime, Washington heavily criticized several European countries for refusing to allow US forces to use NATO bases in its war with Iran.
