World.title: PM Modi pitches India as trusted chipmaking hub
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The AI boom is creating demand for new and reliable chip manufacturing hubs, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said Thursday, pitching India as a destination building the ecosystem that the global semiconductor industry needs.

Inaugurating Semicon India 2026, the PM said AI was changing semiconductor requirements beyond smaller transistors, thereby propelling the importance of chip integration, data movement, heat management and dependable power.

PM Narendra Modi said, âToday if you are working on AI, the challenges are not only about what is inside the chip, but also about what is happening around it.â

These included bringing memory closer to processors and connecting multiple chips to function as one system.

Modi said AI demand had contributed significantly to the growth of more than 20% in the global semiconductor market over the past two years.

âAmid these challenges, what the world now needs most are new and reliable manufacturing locations,â he said, adding that India was preparing itself to meet that need. India had begun the $13.5-billion second phase of its Semiconductor Mission, following up on the $8-billion first phase, Modi said.





Twelve projects had been approved, with the next phase expected to widen participation.

He invited equipment manufacturers and suppliers of chemicals, gases and materials to invest, saying India wanted to strengthen domestic supply chains alongside chipmaking. âWe want the entire ecosystem to grow together,â he said.

He also invited Indian youth conducting research overseas to return to the country to contribute to advanced technology development domestically and urged industry to lead R&D initiatives.

The PM identified compound semiconductors and silicon photonics as priorities for AI infrastructure.

Govt had introduced reforms allowing international companies to collaborate with Indian startups, design companies and OCIowned companies, he said, while seeking to encourage fabless businesses and domestic intellectual property creation.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

PM Modi said Indiaâs chip industry progressed from policy discussions-project announcements to commercial production stages.

Indian plants were supplying customers at home and abroad, while production was beginning at two more plants in Mohali and Surat.

âIt takes decades to build technological capabilities. Wherever semiconductor ecosystems have been built in the world, they have been prepared after decades of effort. But India, with your cooperation, has worked simultaneously on chip design and production, equipment manufacturing, materials ecosystem, testing capability â and has shown success,â he said.

âIndiaâs success in this critical industry would strengthen global supply chains,â Modi said arguing that its significance bettered even as supply chains are being weaponised.

World.title: SC raps CBSE for refusing to exempt Class VI from 3-language policy this year
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Thursday rapped CBSE for being stubborn in its decision to enforce the three-language policy from this year for Class VI students and forced it to reconsider the decision with a clear mandate, camouflaged as a suggestion, to enforce it from next academic year.

CBSE had decided to enforce the three-language policy for all classes from Class VI to X, in which the students were to choose three languages of which two must be indigenous. On SC's request, it reconsidered and agreed to enforce it from Class VI onwards from this year while students in Class VII to X were to be governed by the old policy.

SC had asked CBSE to reconsider exempting students of Class VI this year.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana is dealing with a bunch of petitions challenging the threelanguage policy, including highlighting the inadequacy of textbooks, indigenous subject teachers and infrastructure.

When additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati told the bench that CBSE is disinclined to exempt Class VI this year and argued, âLet the Class VI students start this year as they would have three more years before appearing in Class X board examination,â the bench said, âIt is your cohort who decided that it must be enforced from Class VI without considering the comfort of the Class VI students upon whom you sprung a surprise.





â

âWhen the notification for enforcing the policy came, the student was already in Class VI. Go back and reconsider. Anyway, the academic year will come to an end in a few months. You enforce it for Class VI students from the 2027-28 academic year,â it said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Bhati agreed to take back the decision for reconsideration. The bench said exempting Class VI students from the policy this year would be without prejudice to CBSEâs right to defend the policy.

âThe exemption is purely from the aspect of logistics and balance of convenience,â it said.

SC said, âThere are more contentious issues on what can be considered an indigenous language (Petitioners say English should be considered as one while Centre objects to it) which we will decide later.â

It added, âThere must be some degree of comfort for the students. Those who would be coming to Class VI next year would know in advance that they must choose languages as per the three-language policy.

You can also make it optional for Class VI students with adequate incentives so those who want to conform to the policy can choose to do so.â SC posted the matter for further hearing on Wednesday.

World.title: Kashmir cracks walnut success code, turns to medium-sized, grafted trees
World.content:
KOKERNAG: In Gohan village, around 100km south of Srinagar, Shabir Ahmad was among many harvesting walnuts from a towering tree. The work has become increasingly difficult. âMy back aches now,â Ahmad said.

J&K produces 3.5 lakh tonnes of walnuts annually, around 90% of the countryâs total output.

Like other villagers, Ahmad had no safety gear and he was proud of it. âWe have been doing it for centuries,â said Ahmad, also a clerk at a local court. However, the bravado doesnât help in harvesting seasons. Dr. Mohd Yaqoob Bhat, a surgeon at Paras Hospital in Srinagar, said Valley healthcare units treat dozens of patients each year after falls from walnut trees, some with serious spinal injuries.

âThere is no mechanism to address the issue,â Bhat said.

Ahmadâs younger brother sold one walnut for one rupee and no two fruits are similar. For generations, Kashmirâs walnut trees have been grown from seeds. J&K and Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology (SKUAST) are now promoting medium-sized, grafted walnut trees to bring greater uniformity and help the produce compete globally amid competition from soft-shelled varieties grown in California and Chile.





The initiative aims to replace scattered plantations with organised orchards of known varieties, allowing farmers to grow more trees in the same area and produce walnuts more consistent in size and color.

J&K has about 80,000 hectares under walnut cultivation, most of it made up of seedling-origin trees. âWhen someone plants a walnut seed in the ground, whatever grows becomes a tree. Every tree is a variety of its own,â Ashfaq A.

Pandit, professor and head of fruit science at SKUAST, said. This natural variation, once considered an advantage, has become a challenge in the modern market where buyers seek consistent produce.

Traditional walnut trees can take about 15 years to bear fruit without using pesticides. Unlike traditional seedling-origin trees, grafted walnuts belong to known varieties.

Imtiyaz Ahmad Lone, professor and head of SKUASTâs Walnut Research Centre, said the university released new walnut cultivars and grafting-based cultivation had spread over nearly 90,000 hectares despite lack of subsidies.

Farmers argued, however, that the grafted varieties are no match for the traditional Kashmiri walnut. âIt is no match in taste. The new varieties are brittle, tasteless. They are a no-show,â Mohammad Sultan, a Pulwama farmer in the business for 50 years, said.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Researchers differed. Lone pointed out that grafted trees have early bearing, give faster returns as orchards and nut quality are uniform. âThey have higher productivity and better export potential.

There is a gradual opportunity to replace unproductive seedling trees,â he said.

The transition has impacted walnut woodcraft industries. Walnut trees cannot be cut in J&K without govt permission. The matter was debated in the assembly in March when CM Omar Abdullah opposed a bill allowing landowners to cut walnut trees on private property. Omar defended the restrictions, saying the law served a broader purpose of conserving walnut and chinar trees.

World.title: Flowers at 10,600ft: World’s highest twin fields unveiled in Leh
World.content:
Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers,

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

JAMMU/SRINAGAR: On Prime Minister Narendra Modiâs 76th birthday, Ladakh Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena inaugurated the worldâs highest and Indiaâs largest twin flower fields in Leh, at an altitude of 10,600ft, on Thursday as part of the administrationâs efforts to diversify agriculture, build skills and create new livelihood opportunities in the Union Territory.Spread across 40 acres at Choglamsar and Stakna, the gardens house more than 25 lakh high-value flowers, including 24 lakh Lilium and 1 lakh Gladiolus. The Choglamsar field was developed in just two months, with plantation beginning on July 16 and the first blooms appearing in the first week of Sept. At Stakna, nearly 1.4 lakh lilies were planted in Aug, with the first blooms expected by Oct-end.Saxena said the initiative was the first experiment of its size and nature at such a high altitude in Leh, adding that its successful execution could pave the way for replication elsewhere in Ladakh. The gardens will open to the public on Sept 18, with an entry fee of Rs 25 for adults and Rs 10 for children, officials said.Floriculture, as a high-value agricultural activity, can complement traditional farming, increase cultivatorsâ incomes and create opportunities for employment and entrepreneurship, the LG said. The Choglamsar flower park will serve as a training, demonstration and model floriculture centre for farmers and youth, where Lilium, Gladiolus, Tulips and other ornamental flowers will be cultivated for national and international markets.âThe facility will provide exposure to modern cultivation techniques, scientific farming practices and improved post-harvest management, enabling farmers to acquire the knowledge and skills required to take up floriculture at farm and village levels,â Saxena said. âBesides functioning as a recreational and educational space for residents and tourists, it will create an ecosystem where not only flowers, but also knowledge, skills and enterprises can grow,â he added.

World.title: ‘May your service be accompanied by good health’: Bangladesh PM Rahman wishes PM Modi on birthday
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday on Thursday, as Dhaka seeks to reset ties with New Delhi.

âWarmest birthday wishes to Prime Minister @narendramodi.

Wishing you many happy returns of the day. May your dedicated service to the people of India always be accompanied by good health and high spirit,â Rahman posted on X.

PM Modi responded by thanking Rahman for his message.

âThank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words,â he said.

The exchange comes at a time when Bangladesh is seeking to move away from the strained ties of the previous 18 months.

State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Sunday that Dhaka wanted to âresetâ its relationship with India and establish a new engagement centred on mutual interests.

Relations had deteriorated during Muhammad Yunusâs interim administration, which came to power after the Sheikh Hasina government was toppled in August 2024. Hasina left Bangladesh for India after her ouster, and her continued stay there has remained a major point of friction, with Dhaka repeatedly seeking her extradition.





Rahmanâs Bangladesh Nationalist Party won the February 12 election, held without Hasinaâs Awami League, which has since been disbanded. His government has maintained its demand for Hasinaâs extradition, while the former prime minister has said she plans to return to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.

Dhaka has also indicated that Rahman could visit India once the two governments agree on a suitable time and schedule.

Greeting from across nation and beyond

Rahmanâs message was among birthday greetings sent to PM Modi by political leaders, foreign governments, diplomats and public figures on Thursday.

Russian President Vladimir Putin sent his wishes and, according to the Russian Embassy in New Delhi, described PM Modi as a leader with âgreat authority on the global stageâ. Putin also thanked Modi for the âwarm and cordial welcome and hospitalityâ during his recent visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit.

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the Prime Minister as a âfriendâ and said she looked forward to further strengthening India-Italy relations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Modiâs leadership had âtransformed India into a world powerâ and described the India-Israel relationship as an âunprecedented partnershipâ.

Opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati and Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, joined the birthday wishes.

PM Modi was born on September 17, 1950, in Vadnagar, Gujarat. He became Gujarat chief minister in 2001 and prime minister in 2014, and is set to complete 25 years in public office on October 7.

World.title: Owners face penalties as govt moves to curb stray cattle on highways, e-ways
World.content:
Govt issues SOP to curb stray cattle on highways, allowing fines and penalties for owners.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Owners who abandon cattle on highways and expressways could face fines and penalties, with the road transport ministry issuing a standard operating procedure (SOP) to curb the menace of stray cattle and other animals causing road crashes. States and local authorities will initiate âowner-tracingâ and take steps to recover applicable fees, fines and penalties from owners.The SOP follows a Supreme Court direction to NHAI to devise a structured mechanism for the safe removal of stray animals from national highways and expressways.The âSOP for Safe Removal of Stray Cattle and Other Animals from NHs/Expresswaysâ, issued this week to highway agencies and state govts, designates NHAI, NHIDCL and state PWDs as nodal agencies for removing stray animals from NHs and expressways. They will arrange their safe transportation to shelters, cattle pounds or gaushalas identified by state govts.The highway agencies will identify and mark stretches where stray cattle and other animals are frequently spotted. They will also arrange and bear the cost of transporting the animals to shelters identified and maintained by state and local authorities.States and local authorities will âmaintain cattle-pound records and initiate owner-tracing and action for recovery of applicable fees, fines and penalties under the relevant cattle-trespass legislationâ, as per the SOP.State govts are empowered to initiate action under the The Cattle-Trespass Act of 1871 .State govts can invoke provisions of The Cattle-Trespass Act, 1871 against owners. Section 25 provides for recovery of fines imposed for damage caused by cattle trespassing through the sale of the animals involved. This applies whether the cattle were caught while trespassing or later, and whether they belonged to the offender or were merely in their charge when the offence occurred.Though there is no separate official data on crashes and fatalities caused specifically by stray cattle and other animals. However, in 2024, 19,082 crashes and 8,917 deaths were recorded under the ârun off the roadâ category. The road transport ministry has said such crashes could result from excessive or inappropriate speed, driver distraction, misjudging a curve or attempts to avoid a collision with another road user or an animal.

World.title: West Bengal govt. participates in PM Modi’s birthday celebrations; life-size statue unveiled at BJP office in Kolkata
World.content:
West Bengal government took part in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s birthday celebrations on Thursday (September 17, 2026) by lighting one lakh diyas across Kolkata. A statue of the Prime Minister was also unveiled at the Bharatiya Janata Party office in the capital city.

The State government also observed the PM‘s Birthday as ‘Annapurna Divas’ and launched the PM Vishwakarma Scheme.

“PM Modi said that they have made a list of 50 lakh names in West Bengal for whom houses will be made under the Awas Yojana, women will be made the owners of these houses,” Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari said in his address during the celebrations.

This is the first time West Bengal has joined the Pradhan Mantri Vishwakarma Yojana scheme launched by the Union government. Under this scheme, the government assures to provide support to traditional artisans and craftspeople who work with their hands.

“Here, out of 7,70,000 earlier enrollments, 2,02,000 are currently active... For the time being we are bringing a bill at the Assembly to delegate some of the power to Pachayat Secretaries to make the Vishwakarma Bill a success,” Mr Adhikari said. He added that the previous government did not allow for the central government’s schemes to be implemented in West Bengal.

Life-size statue of Modi at Kolkata BJP office

One of the biggest diya light events was organised in Kolkata on the ghats of Ganga to mark the occasion. Mr. Adhikari also participated in the diya lighting event at Baje Kadamtala Ghat. In another Ganga ghat, MSME Union Minister Jiten Ram Manjhi lit diyas with 400 beneficiaries of the Vishwakarma Yojana.

“A diya of blessings will be lit in every household for Modi ji. That is why we are distributing the diyas for every home... At least 2 crore diyas will be lit across West Bengal,” State Minister Dilip Ghosh said. Such programmes were organised across every district in the State.

BJP State president Samik Bhattacharya unveiled the wax statue of Mr. Modi at the party’s Salt Lake office. The life-size statue was made and gifted to them by artist Susanta Roy.

Later several party leaders along with Mr Bhattacharya went to the Dakshineswar Kali Temple to offer prayers for the PM’s birthday. His birthday was also celebrated at the Kalighat Temple, a place popular with Trinamool chairperson Mamata Banerjee.

Various socio-cultural programs, blood donation camps, and functions at schools were also organised on Thursday (September 17, 2026) to mark the occasion.

World.title: No culture of cut-money in Bengal anymore: PM Modi
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday (September 17, 2026) said that there is no more a culture of cut-money in West Bengal. He made the statement in a virtual address after releasing the fourth instalment of the Annapurna Yojana to women beneficiaries in the State.

“The money is directly transferred in the bank accounts of the women, without any intermediary. Now there is no cut-money in West Bengal,” Mr. Modi said during a virtual address.

Cut-money refers to commission charged by local politicians to help citizens avail benefits of the government schemes. The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leadership, including PM Modi, had promised to stop this corruption in the election campaign of the Assembly elections in the State which the party won.

Speaking about the BJP government in West Bengal, Mr. Modi said that the government believes in “speaking less and working more”.

The Prime Minister, who was addressing the event on his 76th birthday, also added that no eligible women will be deprived of the benefits of Annapurna Yojana in West Bengal. Mr. Modi released the fourth instalment of the cash transfer scheme of ₹3,000 to around 1.5 crore women beneficiaries in West Bengal.

“Within a few days of forming our government in Bengal, work began on the Annapurna Yojana. Today, many women receive financial assistance directly into their bank accounts.... Our government aims to ensure that not a single eligible woman is deprived of the benefits of Annapurna Yojana,” he said in the virtual address.

Mr. Modi said that the Annapurna Yojana is an important effort to strengthen the confidence of Bengal’s women and added that he believes that the women of the State should have both the power to make decisions and the courage to move forward.

Annapurna Yojana was promised by the BJP during the campaign for the West Bengal Assembly polls. The promise was to counter Trinamool Congress government’s Lakshmir Bhandar scheme where over 2.2 crore were getting ₹1500 per month.

After coming to power in May 2026, the BJP government started verification of beneficiaries, something which was criticised by the opposition as a diversion from what the BJP had promised. The Lakshmir Bhandar was a universal scheme, whereas Annapurna Bhandar has an eligibility criterion. There have been some protests with women claiming that they are being denied benefits of the scheme despite being eligible.

The Prime Minister said that the people of Bengal have been deprived of the benefits of many central schemes for a long time. “The BJP is taking forward all the stalled schemes after coming to power,” Mr. Modi said, adding that more than 50 lakh families will be identified and given pucca houses.

“We will all build a new Bengal together,” he added.

World.title: Prince Harry makes first public appearances 'back on British soil'

World.title: FM Nirmala Sitharaman meets Nepalese counterpart Wagle, discusses flood recovery
World.content:
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Thursday (September 17, 2026) met her Nepalese counterpart Swarnim Wagle in New Delhi and discussed the impact of the recent flash floods in Nepal and the country's priorities for reconstruction and rehabilitation.

"The two ministers discussed the impact of the floods and Nepal's priorities for reconstruction and rehabilitation. FM Smt. @nsitharaman conveyed her condolences on the loss of lives in the recent floods in Nepal, and conveyed India's continued support for Nepal's recovery and rebuilding efforts," the Finance Ministry said in a post on X.

The duo also discussed measures to strengthen bilateral economic ties and initiatives to enhance connectivity for deepening trade, investments and people-to-people exchanges.

"Both sides emphasised the importance of further strengthening the trade and economic partnership between India and Nepal," the Ministry said.

Mr. Wagle is on his first official visit to India since assuming office as Nepal's Finance Minister.

Foreign Secretary and the Secretary of the Department of Economic Affairs also joined the meeting.

The discussions come against the backdrop of India's continued engagement with Nepal on economic cooperation, connectivity and development assistance.

World.title: U.S. approves sale of 48 F-35 jets to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
The United States has approved a $24.3 billion sale of 48 F-35 stealth warplanes and related equipment to Saudi Arabia, the U.S. State Department announced on Thursday (September 17, 2026), in a significant boost to the kingdom's forces.

Saudi Arabia has long sought to buy F-35s, but officials from Israel — the only country in the region to operate the jets — have voiced concern about their sale to Riyadh despite a push for the kingdom to normalise relations.

"The proposed sale will improve Saudi Arabia's capability to deter current and future threats by strengthening its homeland defense, and improving interoperability with US forces," the State Department said in a statement.

It "will also augment Saudi Arabia's operational aircraft and enhance its air-to-air, and air-to-ground self-defense capability," it added.

The State Department has notified Congress about the proposed sale, which would require the approval of U.S. lawmakers.

World.title: Nepal flash flood death toll surges to 1,410; over 6,100 still missing
World.content:
The death toll from the devastating flash floods in Nepal surged to 1,410 on Thursday (September 17, 2026), with over 6,100 people still missing, according to the country's disaster management authorities.

Flash floods, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border on August 26, devastated towns and villages in northern and central Nepal.

The Bhotekoshi River, which flows south from the Himalayan border region, carried the floodwaters downstream, sweeping away homes, vehicles, roads and bridges and damaging hydropower projects.

According to the data issued by Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority(NDRRMA) on Thursday evening, 1,410 people have been killed in the floods so far, with 6,145 people still missing.

According to NDRRMA, 364 dead bodies have been recovered from Chitwan district, 232 from Nawalparasi East, 222 from Nawalparasi West, and 203 from Nuwakot.

Similarly, 199 bodies have been recovered from Rasuwa, 78 bodies from Gorkha, 72 bodies from Dhading and 38 bodies from Tanahu.

Two flood victims died in Kathmandu hospitals while undergoing treatment.

So far, 13,756 people have been rescued from the flood-affected areas.

The joint command of security personnel continues to carry out search and rescue operations in the flood-affected areas.

World.title: Satya Niketan building collapse case: Kiran Bedi moves Delhi HC seeking to intervene; Centre opposes
World.content:
Retired IPS officer Kiran Bedi on Thursday (September 17, 2026) approached the Delhi High Court seeking to be made a party in a case concerning the Satya Niketan building collapse, that left seven people dead, saying she wanted to bring forth “critical public domain disclosures” and the “nexus” in the operation of PG hostels.

Additional Solicitor General Chetan Sharma, appearing for the Centre, the Delhi government and the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD), however, opposed Ms. Bedi’s application saying she was pre-judging the matter and sought time to file objections.

“What reply will you file? She is a conscientious citizen of the country. She has administrative experience. The matter is in larger public interest,” a Bench of Chief Justice D.K. Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia told the law officer.

The Court said Ms. Bedi, who also served as the Lieutenant Governor of Puducherry, was seeking to intervene in the case only to assist the court and her “long experience” could always be utilised.

The court gave the authorities three days to file their replies to Ms. Bedi’s plea and listed it for hearing along with the main matter on September 25.

The building at Satya Niketan, which housed a boys’ paying-guest accommodation near the Delhi University’s South Campus, collapsed on September 6 while repair work was under way. Four students were among the seven people who died in the collapse, while several others were injured.

In her application seeking to be made a party in the case, Ms. Bedi said she wanted to bring forth “critical public domain disclosures” on a “nexus between local political representatives, administrative apathy, and the rampant operation of illegal PG hostels being owned and run by the administrators, politicians and their family, associates, etc”.

The application said it was “highly improbable” that local authorities were unaware of the illegal, unsafe accommodations for students, and therefore, it ought to be seen whether the administration knowingly turned a blind eye.

Ms. Bedi said the need of the hour was to constitute a committee under a retired high court judge, comprising public spirited persons and the highest functionaries of the statutory authorities, to submit a detailed report and ensure that such incidents, which have now become a regular feature, are not repeated.

World.title: Russia, China veto U.S. proposal for UN experts to keep monitoring sanctions on Iran
World.content:
Russia and China vetoed a United Nations resolution on Thursday (September 17, 2026) that would have authorised UN experts to keep monitoring sanctions that were reimposed against Iran last year over its nuclear program.

The UN Security Council sanctions are still in effect, which freeze Iran's assets abroad, halt arms deals with Tehran and penalize any development of Iran's ballistic missile program, among other measures.

Using a provision in the 2015 nuclear deal between Iran and major powers France, Germany and the United Kingdom triggered the “snapback” mechanism, which reimposed the sanctions on September 27, 2025. It restored the Security Council sanctions committee and authorised a panel of UN experts to monitor implementation.

The United States drafted a resolution to extend the UN expert panel's mandate for a year, coming as America also pursues a wider campaign to isolate Tehran from its remaining economic partners as the more than six-month-old war in Iran has hit a stalemate. The proposal was defeated by a vote of 11-2, with Somalia and Pakistan abstaining, because of the Russian and Chinese vetoes.

Since Israel and the U.S. struck Iran's nuclear sites in June 2025, UN nuclear inspectors have been unable to verify the status of Iran's stockpile of enriched uranium. According to the UN nuclear watchdog, Iran maintained a stockpile of 440.9 kilograms (972 pounds) of uranium enriched up to 60 per cent purity — a short, technical step away from weapons-grade levels of 90 per cent.

Iran's UN mission thanked China and Russia for vetoing the resolution, saying on social media that the countries “prevented yet another cynical attempt by the United States and its allies to abuse the Security Council for their political purposes.”

U.S. Deputy Ambassador to the UN Jennifer Locetta said the United States wasn't surprised by the vetoes because the experts “would have shined the light" on prohibited cooperation between Iran and its partners.

She said the vetoes are part of a broader effort to prevent expert monitoring of sanctions, and even the appointment of panel members, “to stifle reporting that implicates their own activities in support of rogue regimes.”

In March 2024, a Russian veto ended UN monitoring of sanctions against North Korea over its nuclear program. In Mali, sanctions were terminated, and Locetta said that in Yemen and the Central African Republic expert appointments have been delayed or refused.

While the panel of experts for Iran was authorized a year ago and Secretary-General Antonio Guterres proposed members, they were never approved.

“Without an independent panel of experts, this council loses its principal source of impartial, evidence-based reporting on sanctions violations, creating a monitoring gap that only benefits the Iranian regime and those who profit from evading those measures,” Ms. Locetta warned.

Russian UN Ambassador Vassily Nebenzia reiterated Moscow's claim that the “snapback” of sanctions against Iran was illegal, and therefore the resolution to extend the mandate of the panel of experts “was deeply flawed and did not have any legal basis.”

Russia and China had strongly urged the U.S. and its allies not to put the resolution to a vote, which would only increase tensions in the council, Nebenzia said, but Washington “decided to opt for confrontation.”

French UN Ambassador Jerome Bonnafont, the current council president, said implementing sanctions is “a crucial instrument to encourage Iran” to return to its nuclear obligations. France will study how to ensure sanctions are enforced, he said.

One possibility would be to follow what happened after the North Korea panel of experts was abolished: establishing a monitoring team that includes France, Germany, the UK and the United States.

World.title: Imaan Mazari, husband sent on judicial remand in another case after SC suspends sentences
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Hours after the Supreme Court suspended the sentences of human rights lawyer Imaan Zainab Mazari-Hazir and her husband, Hadi Ali Chattha, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected police’s request for a 30-day physical remand of the couple and sent them to jail on judicial remand.

On January 24, an Islamabad sessions court sentenced Imaan and Hadi to a total of 17 years in jail on multiple charges under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca). The convictions of the couple, who had already been jailed the day before in a separate case, were widely condemned by lawyers and United Nations (UN) experts .

Islamabad ATC Judge Abul Hasnat Muhammad Zulqarnain passed the order after the two accused were produced before the court for a hearing in a case registered against them at Kohsar police station.

Soon after their release, Islamabad police personnel, led by the SSP Operations, reached Adiala jail and arrested the two again in connection with the case registered at Kohsar police station. The police subsequently produced them before the ATC late at night.

Former federal minister Shireen Mazari confirmed the development, saying attempts were being made to keep the couple in jail.

Speaking to Dawn, Imaan’s counsel Riasat Ali Azad also confirmed the development, saying a large contingent of Islamabad police had shifted the couple to Kohsar police station.

The case at the federal capital’s Kohsar police station was registered on March 22, 2025, on the complaint of City Magistrate Ghulam Murtaza Chandio.

Imaan and her husband were accused of chanting anti-government slogans and blocking roads and were nominated by name in the FIR. However, at the time of registration of the case, no section of the Anti-Terrorism Act (ATA) had been added.

The FIR included Section 188 (disobedience of an order lawfully promulgated by a public servant), Section 341 (wrongful restraint), Section 506 (punishment for criminal intimidation), Section 353 (assault or use of criminal force to deter a public servant from discharging their official duty) and Section 186 (obstructing a public servant in the performance of official duties).

SC suspends sentences

Earlier today, the apex court suspended their sentences after a two-judge SC bench, headed by Justice Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Justice Ishtiaq Ibrahim, took up the couple’s appeals against the Islamabad High Court’s (IHC) refusal in February to suspend the sentences.

On Thursday, the SC granted the couple bail against surety bonds of Rs200,000 and ordered their release pending the IHC’s final verdict.

“Both are lawyers and we are keeping their honour,” observed Justice Afghan, but also asked senior counsel Faisal Siddiqui, the couple’s lawyer, to tell the appellants to observe the court’s decorum.

“There is a difference between a lawyer and an ordinary person,” the judge observed.

According to a written order, the SC converted the petitions of both Imaan and Hadi into appeals and suspended the operation of the January 24 conviction.

The court also ordered the release of petitioners — noting they were practising advocates — on bail till the decision of their pending appeals before IHC. The release was subject to furnishing personal surety bonds worth Rs200,000 for each with the SC’s additional registrar (judicial).

The SC will issue a detailed verdict on the case later.

Earlier, the SC had repeatedly adjourned hearings in the case on the grounds that the IHC had fixed their application for suspension of sentence along with the main appeal.

During Thursday’s hearing, Siddiqui argued that the SC had issued its first order on May 12 in which the IHC was asked to decide the applicants’ petition for suspension of sentence as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of two weeks.

On May 12, the SC ordered the IHC to decide Imaan and Hadi’s sentence suspension pleas within two weeks. Despite the May 26 deadline having already passed, the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) challenged the SC order and sought its withdrawal.

During the proceedings, Siddiqui also read out the order sheets from various IHC hearings.

At one point, the SC directed Additional Attorney General (AAG) Rana Asadullah Khan, who was standing at the rostrum, to take a seat, adding that the court will hear Siddiqui first.

“Let him sit, though he has certainly worn us out,” Siddiqui quipped and cited former chief justice Asif Saeed Khosa’s remarks that a case would only be adjourned upon the death of a judge or a lawyer.

The counsel regretted that the IHC adjourned the case multiple times and that his clients’ request for an early hearing was rejected by the high court’s registrar office.

“What transpired at the high court came as a surprise to us,” the counsel said.

“These days are an era of surprises,” remarked Justice Ibrahim.

During the hearing, the AAG contended that the IHC has not yet issued any adverse ruling, adding that seven opportunities were provided in the trial court.

He highlighted that the judicial forum for the suspension of a sentence under Section 426 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) was the high court.

Justice Afghan observed that the IHC always cited the SC directives for early disposal of the case but does not act upon them.

The judge also asked AAG Khan whether he would give any assurance that proceedings would be held at the next IHC hearing, to which the latter replied that he cannot represent any high court judge in the SC.

Later, the SC suspended the sentence of the applicants and ordered their release on bail, pending the IHC’s final verdict.

In their applications, the applicants had stated that it was a settled policy of the SC that criminal matters have to be given priority, especially when the matters pertain to bail or suspension of sentence.

Moreover, in Section 7 of the Supreme Court (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2023, it was expressly stated that any application pleading urgency shall be fixed for hearing within a period of 14 days.

The application contended that Imaan was a young female lawyer and has remained incarcerated for a long period of time in a case where conviction was the “result of a sham trial”.

The case

Imaan and Hadi have been in jail since their arrest on January 23 in a case registered against them for protesting outside the IHC and allegedly manhandling the IHC Bar Association (IHCBA) president. The arrest prompted criticism by rights bodies, politicians and journalists, who stressed the couple’s right to a fair trial.

Just a day later, a sessions court convicted Imaan and Hadi in the social media posts case.

It sentenced the duo to 10 years’ imprisonment under Section 10 (cyber terrorism), five years’ imprisonment under Section 9 (glorification of an offence) and two years’ imprisonment under Section 26-A (false and fake information) of Peca.

All sentences were to run concurrently.

The case stemmed from a complaint filed on Aug 12, 2025 by the assistant director (investigating officer) at the NCCIA Islamabad, before the Federal Investigation Agency’s Cybercrime Reporting Centre.

The complaint accused Imaan of disseminating and “propagating narratives that align with hostile terrorist groups and proscribed organisations”, while her husband was implicated for reposting some of her posts.

The first information report (FIR) in the case alleged that the two held security forces responsible for cases of missing persons in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan.

It also stated that they had portrayed the armed forces as ineffective against proscribed groups, including the banned outfits Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP).

Judge Majoka had indicted Imaan and Hadi in the case on Oct 30, 2025 and issued arrest warrants for the couple on Nov 5, 2025. The judge then reissued arrest warrants for them in January after repeated non-appearances.

After being convicted, the couple challenged the sentences by filing separate appeals in the IHC on February 7. Taking up those appeals and sentence suspension pleas on February 19, the IHC issued notices to the respondents but refused to suspend the sentences.

On April 30, Imaan and Hadi moved a separate appeal before the SC against the IHC’s February order. They sought an early hearing of the plea in June, after which notices were issued on July 6.

After the SC’s intervention, the IHC finally declared the jailed couple’s pleas seeking suspension of sentences as admissible on July 25. Days later, Imaan moved the SC again seeking an early hearing of the challenge against the IHC order.

Additional input by Mohammad Asghar

World.title: Govt lowers petrol price by Rs0.43 per litre, raises HSD by Rs3.47 per litre
World.content:
The government on Thursday cut the price of petrol by Rs0.43 per litre but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.47 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.79 per litre while HSD will cost Rs424.92 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on Sept 18 (Friday).

According to Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (OGRA), the increase is primarily linked to higher petrol and diesel prices in the international market.

The regulator said the prices were revised based on international market rates, premiums and other relevant factors.

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices, including requiring markets to close by 9pm and cutting fuel allocations for official vehicles by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

A statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said owners of two- and three-wheelers would receive relief of Rs100 per litre on a monthly quota of 20 litres, while owners of vehicles up to 800cc would receive the same relief on a monthly quota of 30 litres.

On July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Markets to close at 9pm as govt reintroduces austerity measures for fuel conservation
World.content:
The federal government reintroduced austerity measures on Thursday in an effort to conserve fuel amid renewed tensions in the Middle East, setting 9pm as the time for closing markets and reducing fuel provision for official vehicles by 50 per cent for a period of three months.

The measures are to be implemented with immediate effect, the Cabinet Division’s notification detailing the government’s directives said.

According to the Sept 17 notification, seen by Dawn, businesses and commercial establishments are to close at following timings:

Shops, markets, shopping malls and bazaars, as well as departmental, grocery, general and kiryana stores are to close by 9pm

Marriage halls, marquees and all other commercial places where festive events are held are to close by 10pm

Restaurants, cafés, eateries, and food outlets, as well as standalone fruit and vegetable shops are to close by 11pm. Takeaway and home delivery services are exempted from the restriction

Pharmacies, medical and medical supplies’ stores, medical laboratories, clinics, hospitals, standalone bakeries, standalone tandoors, standalone milk and dairy shops, fuel and CNG stations, electrical vehicle charging stations, gyms, sports facilities and sports/padel courts, IT companies and call centres are also exempted from any time restrictions.

Moreover, just a single dish should be served at all marriage-related functions or events, the notification said.

The Cabinet Division also detailed comprehensive instructions for government entities and officials.

These include the reduction in fuel provision by 50pc for official vehicles for three months.

Vehicles of armed forces, civil armed forces, vehicles in use of law enforcement agencies, those used for essential services and those in use of the Federal Board of Revenue are excluded from this restriction barring those of administrative or non-operational formations of these entities.

This measure is also not applicable in the case of development projects, according to the notification.

The government has also announced a 5pc reduction in the budget for non-employee related expenditures for FY2026-27, with deduction to be made on a monthly basis.

“This measure will also apply in the case of foreign missions and the officers/officials, belonging to any occupational group or service, posted in these missions; however, obligations relating to their rents, educational fees and medical care arrangements will be met,” the notification read, adding that this measure too was not applicable in case of development projects.

According to the notification, the government also imposed a complete ban on the purchase of vehicles of all types, with the restriction not applicable to development projects.

It also prohibited the purchase of all durable goods, except IT-related equipment and services, while clarifying that the measure would not apply to development projects.

It further imposed a three-month ban on foreign visits and travel, including obligatory trips for government officials. The restriction, however, would not apply to scholarships offered by international development partners, or to training and courses arranged through the Economic Affairs Division or under institutional agreements of the Government of Pakistan.

According to the notification, Pakistan’s ambassador or high commissioner concerned would represent the country at obligatory and important events during the period.

However, in case of “unavoidable visits” all ministers, advisors, ministers of state, special assistants to the premier, parliamentary and government functionaries shall “travel only in economy class”.

The government further directed that official meetings will be preferably held through teleconferencing, except intra-city meetings.

“No official dinners shall be hosted, except in the case of visiting foreign delegations,” the notification added.

The notification also prohibited all government-funded official seminars, trainings and conferences. However, where such events were deemed unavoidable, government facilities, including auditoriums and committee rooms, would be used to host them.

It further said requests for exemptions from any of the measures could be considered on a case-by-case basis by the Committee for Monitoring and Implementation of Fuel Conservation and Additional Austerity Measures. The committee would then submit its recommendations to the prime minister for approval.

Earlier this week, Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said that the government was considering reviving austerity measures introduced during a previous fuel conservation drive amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East.

The government had earlier imposed austerity measures on March 9 to mitigate the impact of the ongoing US-Iran war. These included a 50 per cent cut in fuel allowances for official vehicles, salary cuts for lawmakers, and a partial work-from-home policy in the public sector.

The government ended the measures on June 19, except for market timings.

The move comes amid renewed hostilities in the Middle East, which have disrupted major oil supply routes and led to a rise in fuel prices.

In addition to the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz stemming from the US-Iran war, trade through Bab al-Mandab — which has become a vital route for Saudi oil exports in recent months — is also facing a growing threat from Houthi rebels.

World.title: PM’s fuel subsidy scheme faces first-day hurdles at petrol pumps
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The much-touted fuel subsidy scheme launched by the prime minister faced snags on Thursday, the first day of its nationwide rollout, as many petrol pumps declined to honour the digital app, claiming they lacked the system needed to provide petrol at Rs100 per litre less.

After receiving several complaints in this regard, Information Technology Minister Shaza Fatima visited various fuel stations in Rawalpindi to ensure that subsidised petrol was available to registered consumers.

A day earlier, the Pakistan Petroleum Dealers Association (PPDA) expressed concerns that its members were unaware of the subsidy disbursement mechanism and feared they would have to run from pillar to post to recover the amount.

However, to resolve the matter, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik, along with officials from the relevant ministries, held a meeting with the PPDA on Thursday to discuss the mechanism for implementing the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme.

PPDA Chairman Malik Khuda Baksh led the delegation, which joined the meeting via video link.

The State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) briefed the participants on the reimbursement mechanism and assured them that claims submitted under the scheme would be processed within 48 hours, ensuring timely payments to participating petroleum dealers.

The Ministry of IT and Telecommunications briefed the participants on the digital system developed to implement the scheme.

The meeting was also informed that a dedicated control room had been established to assist petrol pumps and address their queries and complaints. Petrol pumps can contact the control room at 9772 for assistance.

The meeting was further informed that funds for three months had been earmarked for the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme, with Rs25 billion for the first month already provided to SBP to facilitate timely reimbursement under the scheme.

The PPDA chairman said the Prime Minister’s Fuel Relief Scheme was welcomed by petroleum dealers, but a lack of information about the disbursement of subsidy amounts was creating confusion among its members.

“We assure you that all our members across the country will support the PM’s fuel relief scheme,” Khuda Baksh said.

During the meeting, the petroleum minister appreciated the cooperation extended by petroleum dealers and emphasised the importance of close coordination among all stakeholders for the effective, transparent and timely implementation of the relief initiative.

OCAC warns of disruption

In another development, the Oil Companies Advisory Committee (OCAC) warned the government of disruption to the oil supply chain if Rs67 billion in price differential claims (PDC) pending since March 2026 were not settled.

In a letter to the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) chairman, the OCAC claimed that the pending PDC amount was equivalent to five imported cargoes of petrol.

The letter, written by OCAC Secretary General Dr Nazir Abbas Zaidi, was forwarded to the petroleum minister and the Petroleum Division secretary. It said oil companies were now unable to finance an uninterrupted fuel supply chain due to Rs66.7 billion in outstanding PDCs.

The OCAC said the situation had been further aggravated by the evolving geopolitical environment and potential disruptions to regional supply routes, including the East-West Pipeline.

The oil companies warned that the country could face significant supply-side challenges under the current regional scenario, while the oil industry’s liquidity continued to deplete due to a lack of support from the authorities.

“Any resulting supply-chain disruption must not be on account of the oil industry,” the OCAC said in the letter.

Despite repeated communications and extensive verification and audit processes, the OCAC had requested settlement by June 8, 2026, but the matter remained unresolved, it added.

“We urge Ogra to urgently conclude the verification process and release all verified and approved claims, including the approved premium differential claims relating to Motor Spirit (petrol) imports during the recent geopolitical crisis, referring to the situation arising following the US-Israeli attack on Iran at the end of February 2026.”

The OCAC said oil marketing companies (OMCs) had consistently supported the government, particularly when fuel security and uninterrupted supplies were at stake.

“Yet today, the same industry is facing an acute and worsening liquidity crisis and effectively being required to finance the supply chain while its own liquidity is being progressively drained,” the OCAC said, inviting government functionaries to meet its members at its head office in Karachi.

The OCAC also reminded the government of the need to revise OMC margins, adding that they were last revised in September 2023 and had remained unchanged despite significant increases in operating, financing, technology, regulatory and compliance costs.

The letter added that dealer margins were increased by Rs1.34 per litre in August 2026, while the approved Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins remained to be notified and implemented.

“Unlike dealers, OMCs carry the full responsibility for product procurement, import financing, inventory management, logistics and ensuring product availability across the country, in addition to meeting ever-expanding regulatory and digitisation requirements, with implementation timelines being progressively compressed,” the letter said. It demanded immediate notification and implementation of the Rs1.22 per litre increase in OMC margins and the establishment of a predictable mechanism for periodic margin revisions.

World.title: PM Shehbaz reaches London before heading to New York for UNGA session
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday reached London for a two-day stopover before proceeding to the United States to attend the high-level segment of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York.

According to a source in the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), the premier would proceed to the US on Saturday to attend the UNGA session.

The source said the prime minister was likely to return to the country on Sept 27 or 28 after attending the UNGA session and would again stop over in London for a day or two.

“In fact, travelling from Pakistan to the US is quite a long journey, therefore, PM Shehbaz opted to stay somewhere, preferably in London,” the source added.

According to the Foreign Office, Prime Minister Shehbaz is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly on Sept 25.

“On the sidelines of the UN session, he is expected to hold bilateral meetings with world leaders and participate in high-level events,” the FO said.

The prime minister will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, federal ministers and senior government officials during the New York leg of the visit.

“The premier will present Pakistan’s perspective on regional and global developments and highlight the country’s priorities at the UNGA,” it said.

The official theme of the 81st session is ‘Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations That Delivers for All’, and the UNGA debate is expected to run from Sept 22 to 26, with a final sitting on Sept 28.

However, ongoing fighting between Washington and Tehran is expected to feature prominently in discussions among world leaders, particularly over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, regional stability and the possibility of finding a diplomatic way out of the confrontation.

The premier is expected to highlight Pakistan’s efforts to find a peaceful solution to the ongoing US-Iran war.

World.title: Pakistan, China reaffirm consensus at inaugural Boundary Joint Commission meeting
World.content:
The inaugural meeting of the Pakistan-China Boundary Joint Commission (BJC) concluded in Islamabad on Thursday, with both sides reaffirming their consensus and agreeing on a framework for future cooperation under the commission.

According to the Foreign Office (FO), the meeting was held in Islamabad on Sept 16 and 17, marking the formal launch of the commission. The BJC was envisaged under the 2013 China-Pakistan Agreement on the Boundary Management System.

“Both sides described the establishment of the commission as a vital milestone in further strengthening the Pakistan-China All-Weather Strategic Cooperative Partnership,” the FO said.

According to the statement, discussions at the inaugural meeting covered a wide range of matters related to border management and cooperation, including cross-border coordination, the movement of goods and people, joint border surveys and people-to-people linkages.

The meeting concluded with the signing of the minutes, reaffirming the two sides’ consensus and setting out a framework for future cooperation under the commission, the statement said.

“Both sides agreed to hold the next meeting of the commission in China on mutually convenient dates,” the FO said.

The Pakistan delegation was led by Bilal Mahmood Chaudhary, Director General (China) at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, while the Chinese delegation was led by Li Ya, Deputy Director General of the Department of Boundary and Ocean Affairs at China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

Other representatives from the ministries of foreign affairs, defence, interior, commerce and communications, as well as customs, survey and other boundary management authorities, also attended the meeting.

The commission has its origins in the 2013 Agreement on the Boundary Management System, signed during the visit of then Chinese Premier Li Keqiang to Islamabad. Article 45 of the agreement provides for the establishment of the joint commission to oversee the implementation of border management arrangements.

The mechanism will provide an institutional framework for dealing with practical issues along the border, including the maintenance and inspection of the boundary, joint surveys, boundary marker issues, the management of cross-border facilities and the handling of incidents involving the border.

World.title: Salman Akram Raja says released after PTI claims detention by Islamabad police
World.content:
PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja on Thursday said he was “released” after being briefly detained, with his party claiming he was held by Islamabad police.

In a post on X at 4:39pm, the PTI claimed that Raja, Latasob Satti and “others were unlawfully abducted” when they were on their way to Kotli Sattian to attend a PTI worker’s funeral. A post on Latasob’s Facebook account said his son Ikhlaq Ahmad Satti was also held.

The PTI said they were then transferred to Nilore police station in Islamabad, alleging that “abductions and arrests were ongoing to prevent people from attending the funeral”.

In a subsequent post at 5:32pm, Raja said he, Latasob, Ikhlaq and their “several friends were released after being kept in detention for four hours”.

“The only objective was to prevent us from attending late Ijaz Satti’s funeral. The fear of the public has stripped the decision-makers of their reason and sense,” the PTI secretary general contended, adding that “human rights have become meaningless”.

Latasob, a retired major, also shared a picture on X of him and the PTI leaders, saying they had been released.

PTI Chairman Gohar Ali Khan strongly condemned the alleged detention.

“For the last few days, about 700 workers have been arrested,” Gohar claimed, adding that arrest warrants have also been issued against MNAs and MPAs.

“This is all illegal. This must end now,” he wrote.

Earlier in the day, Raja had addressed a press conference alongside PTI leader Taimur Saleem Jhagra.

The PTI has been holding party activities to mobilise supporters for the PTI’s nationwide protest scheduled for September 27, with Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi touring Punjab this week.

During his visit, the KP CM not only alleged he was “ abducted ” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside, but also claimed a man was sent to kill him.

The Punjab government had swiftly refuted the claims of arrest, while the Wazirabad police clarified that the man accused by Afridi was a police constable deployed on security duty for the CM.

The Punjab government has imposed a ban on gatherings across the province from September 13 to 17.

Earlier this week, district authorities had also issued preventive detention orders against dozens of PTI workers under Section 3 of the Maintenance of Public Order, including 31 in one Punjab notification and a further 14 in Toba Tek Singh.

The administrations of the twin cities of Rawalpindi and Islamabad had already begun preparations to counter the PTI’s announced march to the capital, including a request for the detention of activists, arranging containers, seeking additional personnel and procuring anti-riot gear.

On Wednesday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi visited various checkpoints in Attock connecting Punjab to KP to review security arrangements.

World.title: 'A chief minister's trips are never personal': Maryam claps back at criticism over use of govt aircraft
World.content:
Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz on Thursday shot back at criticism over her use of an official aircraft to attend a family event in London, claiming that a chief minister’s trips “are never personal” and insisting she had borne all trip-related expenses.

CM Maryam came under scrutiny when it emerged that she used the provincial government jet to make a private visit to London, with opposition leaders questioning the use of an official aircraft for a family event.

However, Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari has denied the allegation, also insisting that the trip was paid for “out of her own pocket”.

Addressing a ceremony in Multan, the chief minister addressed the issue, noting criticism “directed at Maryam Nawaz’s plane”.

“It is not Maryam Nawaz’s plane; it is the chief minister’s plane. Maryam Nawaz is not going to take it to Raiwind [..] all four chief ministers have this facility,” she said.

She said she had served Punjab for two-and-a-half years. “I wake up, I go to work and come back in the evening [..] sometimes, I am working till so late that I fall asleep with my iPad or phone in my hand”.

The chief minister said that if she promised people a project, “Maryam always delivers double of that,” referring to herself in the third person.

“If she has committed 1,000 buses, she will give 5,000 [..] but sometimes for these projects, sometimes I have to go places — by cars or by plane [..] was I not on the rescue boats when catastrophic floods hit Punjab in 2025,” she said.

Noting that the chief ministers of all four provinces availed the facility, she said, “It is available to everyone, but the criticism is directed only at Maryam Nawaz”.

“Today, as I was coming here, I thought since there has been so much criticism, perhaps I should go by Qingqi or motorcycle, or if there is a metro bus I can take till here from Lahore,” she quipped.

She then cautioned the audience to be wary that “the criticism is not aimed at me, [but] rather [at] Punjab’s development and growth. It is directed at the mirror we hold to them [other provinces] every day.”

CM Maryam said that for the past two and a half years, she had been eager to see other provinces say they were doing better than Punjab.

She further held that the “Rs9 billion jet” was not hers, but rather belonged to the office of the chief minister.

“Tomorrow, if I go to Sargodha and have to go to Rawalpindi [..] How will I get around?” she questioned, stressing that the “most precious resource for a CM is their time”.

She said that she was heavily criticised solely “because I am doing the work and have left the others in a position where they have to save face”.

CM Maryam said her government had invested “Rs300bn in the Apni Chhat Apna Ghar initiative, Rs200bn in Green Buses [..] we are building the world’s biggest cancer hospital”.

“What have you done?” the chief minister asked.

Taking note of the scrutiny around her daughter’s graduation ceremony, she insisted that she had borne the expenses, with the total bill amounting to Rs27.5 million.

“A chief minister or prime minister is never on leave, and none of their visits is personal. I am working while I am on the plane. I work wherever I am,” CM Maryam claimed.

She further contended that, given the nature of her role, she could not afford to lose contact with her government at any time.

“If I lose contact with my government on an eight-hour flight and if there is an issue, who is going to handle it?” she asked.

Addressing the gathering, CM Maryam held up a “receipt” of the expenses on her phone.

CM Maryam said she did not owe “these vloggers and YouTubers a justification”; however, she maintained, “I would still present an explanation in the court of the public.”

She said that when her tenure ends, “I will not be taking this plane home with me”; however, the chief minister maintained that her trips to Brazil, Japan, China or Türkiye were undertaken “so I could showcase my government’s progress.”

“So, yes, I hope that I get to go again on the plane,” she said.

CM Maryam recalled that the day she was set to return to Pakistan, several commercial flights were cancelled due to an issue with the United Kingdom’s air traffic control system.

“People travelling by commercial flights had to extend their stay by five to six days, and if I did not have the plane, I would have been stuck and lost five to six days. That is not just five to six days for Maryam Nawaz but five to six projects for the people of Punjab,” she said.

“I don’t have time to waste,” CM Maryam said, claiming that she often worked till midnight.

“I then wake up at 8am and come back to work. Every waking moment, my office is with me, whether I am in Murree or London.”

In response to the criticism, she further said, “Kids, keep at it; may God give you more success in your business. I don’t owe you an answer; I am answerable only to the people.”

The chief minister also took a jibe at Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi over his recent visit to Lahore, without naming him.

“As you saw, some people from KP came to Punjab; he was sitting on the roadside, but no one barely recognised the individual,” CM Maryam remarked.

She noted that the visit was “so unsuccessful” that she had to “scold” her deputy commissioners “for not being able to scrounge up at least 400-500 people for a welcome, but even they could not find anyone willing to come”.

CM Maryam said that the “individual from KP” was making statements questioning the government’s legitimacy. However, he failed to get people’s attention, she added.

“Instead, he sat in a police vehicle forcibly and attempted to stage an abduction. He thought perhaps the act would create some drama,” in reference to the KP CM’s claim that he was “abducted” by authorities in Lahore and later “thrown” by the roadside. Punjab government has denied the allegation.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.
